magnet.w: A rooftop on the Magnet building that looks straight down on the Scramble Crossing from the corner diagonally opposite the station. It reopened in March 2026 after a refit, as a lounge with a viewing deck over the crossing.
magnet.t: ¥1,800 each including one drink. Card only, no cash. 10:00 to 22:00, last entry 21:30.
magnet.m: MAGNET by SHIBUYA109 Crossing View rooftop

hikarie.l: 渋谷ヒカリエ 11F スカイロビー
hikarie.w: A free indoor viewing lobby on the 11th floor of the Hikarie tower, on the east side of Shibuya Station. Big windows look west over the station, the trains and the Scramble Crossing.
hikarie.t: Free. 07:00 to midnight. Take the lifts from the B3 to 5F shopping floors.

shibuya-yokocho.w: A long food hall of small counters on the ground floor of Miyashita Park, directly below the hotel. Each counter serves food from a different region of Japan, with shared tables, lanterns and a loud, cheerful crowd at night.
shibuya-yokocho.t: 11:00 to 05:00, Sunday to 23:00. Stalls vary. Turn up and find seats, no booking.

uobei.l: 魚べい 渋谷道玄坂店
uobei.w: A fast sushi bar where you order on a touch screen and each plate shoots to your seat on a little express track. Cheap, quick and fun rather than fine dining.
uobei.t: About ¥110 a plate. 11:00 to midnight. Expect a short queue at peak times.

ebisu-yokocho.w: A covered lane of tiny izakaya and bars a few minutes from Ebisu Station. Yakitori, oden, fresh fish and wine, all at shared counters. Busy with locals after work.
ebisu-yokocho.t: Cash only. Most stalls about 17:00 to 04:00, earlier close on Sunday. One stop from Shibuya on the Yamanote line.

tower-rec.l: タワーレコード渋谷店
tower-rec.w: A nine-storey music store, one of the largest in the world, a few minutes from the hotel. Renovated in early 2026 with bigger J-pop and K-pop floors, photo spots and a craft beer bar on 6F.

daikanyama.w: A calm, low-rise neighbourhood of design shops and cafés one stop south of Shibuya. T-Site is the centrepiece: a bookshop in three linked pavilions, strong on design, art, travel and magazines, with a lounge café upstairs.
daikanyama.t: Bookshop 09:00 to 22:00. One stop on the Tōyoko line, or a 15 minute walk from the hotel through back streets.

nakameguro.w: A canal-side neighbourhood of small boutiques and cafés along the Meguro River. At its far end is the Starbucks Reserve Roastery, a four-floor Kengo Kuma building where they roast on site, with a cocktail bar and tea bar.
nakameguro.t: Roastery 07:00 to 22:00, last orders 21:30. A 10 minute walk on from Daikanyama, so the two pair up well.

yoyogi.w: A big open park right next to Meiji Jingū: lawns, a pond, ginkgo trees and people practising music and dance. On Sundays the rockabilly dancers in leather and quiffs perform near the Harajuku entrance.
yoyogi.t: Free and always open. Enter from the gate beside Harajuku Station.

path.w: A small Tomigaya bistro that turns into one of Tokyo's best loved breakfast spots each morning. The order is the Dutch pancake, baked to order in a pan and topped with cured ham, burrata and maple syrup. It takes about 30 minutes, so get coffee and a croissant while you wait.
path.t: Breakfast 08:00 to about 14:00 (last orders around 14:00). Closed Monday, and some listings also say Tuesday, so Sunday is your day. Walk-in only, expect a queue: be there by 08:00. Mid priced.

fuglen.l: フグレン トウキョウ
fuglen.w: The Tokyo outpost of an Oslo café, set in a tiny corner shop full of 1950s Norwegian furniture. Light roasted coffee is the draw, with a bench out the front for people watching on a quiet Tomigaya street. In the evening it switches to cocktails.
fuglen.t: Daily 07:00 to 23:00 Mon and Tue, to 01:00 other nights. Walk-in. Little food, so grab pastries first from 365日 bakery around the corner (07:00 to 19:00; it had a renovation closure in mid 2026, check before you go).

maisen.l: とんかつ まい泉 青山本店
maisen.w: Tokyo's most famous tonkatsu house, set in a converted 1930s public bathhouse just off Omotesando. Thick pork cutlets in a light, crisp panko crust, served with shredded cabbage, rice, miso soup and their own sweet sauce. The kurobuta black pork loin is the one to order.
maisen.t: Daily 11:00 to 22:00, last orders 21:00. About ¥2,000 to ¥3,000 a head. Walk-in, or book online through Tabelog in English. Expect a short wait at 12:30 on a Saturday.

afuri.w: A modern ramen shop famous for its yuzu shio ramen: a clear chicken broth, bright with yuzu citrus, topped with chargrilled pork. Lighter than the rich pork ramen you see everywhere. You order and pay at a ticket machine with an English option.
afuri.t: Daily, roughly 11:00 to 22:30 (some listings say from 10:00). No bookings. About ¥1,000 to ¥2,000. Cards and Suica accepted.

motomura.l: 牛かつ もと村 原宿店
motomura.w: Beef cutlet, crumbed and flash fried so it stays rare inside, then finished to your liking on a little hot stone at your seat. Served as a set with barley rice, cabbage, potato salad and miso soup. A basement counter of about ten seats.
motomura.t: Open daily, 11:00 to 22:00 at last report (2022, confirm on Google Maps). No bookings. Sets from about ¥1,300 to ¥2,200. Queues are long at peak, but 14:00 on a Monday is the quiet window.

uogashi.l: 寿司 魚がし日本一 渋谷道玄坂店
uogashi.w: A standing sushi bar where chefs make each piece in front of you and pass it across the counter. You order a few pieces at a time, eat, and order more. Fast, fresh and cheap, the way office workers eat sushi in Tokyo.
uogashi.t: Mon to Fri 11:00 to 23:00, Sat 11:00 to 22:00, Sun 11:00 to 21:30. Walk-in. English menu, or point. About ¥1,500 to ¥3,000 a head.

shogun-burger.w: Your wagyu burger. The patty is coarsely ground Japanese black wagyu, never frozen and cooked to order, with a house wagyu sauce. Run by a yakiniku family from Toyama, so the beef is the point. Skin on fries and free refill soft drinks.
shogun-burger.t: Daily 11:30 to 23:00, last orders 22:00. No bookings. Cashless only: cards, Suica, PayPay. About ¥2,000 to ¥3,000 a head.

sushi-ten.w: A proper omakase sushi counter without the months-long wait or the ¥40,000 bill. The chef serves about 20 courses of nigiri and small dishes one at a time across the counter, explaining each fish as it comes. Friendly, lively and very used to first timers.
sushi-ten.t: Dinner 17:00 to 23:00, open weekends. Omakase ¥9,900, or Full Omakase with drinks ¥13,200. 90 minute seating. Book in English on TableCheck (card required, full charge for same day cancels). Cashless. Shibuya Stream 3F.

kaikaya.w: A loud, happy seafood izakaya up the hill in Maruyamachō, decked out like a surf shack. The owner cooks fish Japanese style with a few Western twists: tuna neck grilled like spare ribs, fish carpaccio, crab in spring roll pastry. Lots of other travellers and a staff who love to chat.
kaikaya.t: Dinner 17:00 to 22:30, closed Wednesday. Bookings are for set courses only, ¥5,800 to ¥12,000 plus tax, on OpenTable in English. Day of cancellation fee ¥8,000 a head.
kaikaya.m: Kaikaya by the Sea 23-7 Maruyamacho Shibuya

sg-club.l: ザ エスジー クラブ
sg-club.w: Bartender Shingo Gokan's bar, named among Asia's 50 Best Bars nine years running (No. 23 in 2024). Upstairs, Guzzle is a relaxed walk-in bar with playful drinks like a parmesan pisco sour. Downstairs, Sip is a dim speakeasy with a shoe shine stand.
sg-club.t: Daily from 17:00 until late (01:00 or later). Guzzle on the ground floor is walk-in with no cover charge. Sip in the basement wants a booking and adds a service charge. English menu.

celavi.w: A rooftop restaurant and sky bar on the 17th and 18th floors of Tokyu Plaza Shibuya, right above the station. You look straight down onto the Scramble and across the lights of the city. A sister to the famous rooftop at Marina Bay Sands.
celavi.t: Restaurant and Skybar 11:00 to 23:00, last entry 22:00. Smart casual: no sportswear or thongs. Book a bar spot online on their site. The late night club lounge (from 22:00, closed Monday) has a cover charge.
celavi.m: CE LA VI Tokyo Tokyu Plaza Shibuya

trench.w: A tiny Ebisu speakeasy that has specialised in absinthe and old herbal liqueurs since 2010. Eight seats at a counter, vintage European fittings, and inventive drinks. No. 53 on the extended Asia's 50 Best Bars list for 2026.
trench.t: Daily 19:00 to 02:00. Walk-in only and very small, so go early or try again later. Cards and cash.

jbs.w: A one man listening bar up a narrow stair in Dōgenzaka. The owner, Kobayashi-san, has over 10,000 records lining the walls and plays them on a serious hi-fi, propping up each sleeve so you can see what is on. Whisky, quiet chat and great music.
jbs.t: Open daily, usually from 14:00 or 19:00 until 23:00. Hours vary. No cover charge, cheap drinks. Bring cash. Keep voices low.

fuunji.w: A small counter just off the south side of Shinjuku Station that many rate as Tokyo's best tsukemen. Thick noodles come cold beside a dense chicken and fish dipping broth. Ask for soup at the end to thin what is left into a drinkable bowl.
fuunji.t: 11:00 to 15:00 and 17:00 to 21:00, closes early if sold out. Closed Sundays and public holidays, so Monday is fine. No bookings, expect a queue. Noodles in 200g, 300g or 400g.

tsunahachi.l: 天ぷら 新宿つな八 総本店
tsunahachi.w: A Shinjuku institution frying tempura in sesame oil since the 1920s, in an old wooden house two streets from Shinjuku-sanchōme. Sit at the counter and the prawns, fish and vegetables come out of the oil one at a time. The anago (sea eel) is the house signature.
tsunahachi.t: Open daily, about 11:00 to 22:30. Lunch about ¥2,500, dinner about ¥4,000 a head. Walk-in: counter seats turn over fast.

nagi-goldengai.l: すごい煮干ラーメン凪 新宿ゴールデン街店 本館
nagi-goldengai.w: A tiny ramen shop up a steep stair on the second floor of an old wooden Golden Gai house. The broth is boiled for 12 hours from dried sardines, so it is intensely fishy and savoury, with a mix of curly and wide flat noodles.
nagi-goldengai.t: Open 24 hours. Niboshi ramen ¥1,350. Walk-in, a handful of seats, so a short wait at night.

takano-parlour.l: タカノフルーツパーラー 新宿本店
takano-parlour.w: The parlour two floors under Takano, Shinjuku's famous luxury fruit shop. It is where Tokyo goes for the fruit parfait: tall glasses layered with perfect seasonal fruit and cream. The muskmelon parfait is the showpiece; the mixed fruit one is the sensible order.
takano-parlour.t: B2F, Takano Shinjuku Honten. 11:00 to 21:00, last orders 20:30, daily (at last report in 2022, check on Google Maps). Parfaits from about ¥1,100, muskmelon about ¥3,080. Walk-in.

kakiden.w: A Kyoto style kaiseki restaurant across four floors of a building beside Shinjuku Station's east exit. More than 40 years old, with a sign written by the novelist Kawabata Yasunari and a tea ceremony tradition. Seasonal courses of small, beautiful dishes, in tatami rooms or at tables.
kakiden.t: Dinner 17:00 to 22:00, last orders 20:00. Open daily. Dinner courses about ¥11,000 (Flower) and ¥16,500 (Snow). Book online in English through AutoReserve. Full charge for same day cancels.

benfiddich.l: バー ベンフィディック
benfiddich.w: A dim, 17 seat counter on the ninth floor of a plain office block in Nishi-Shinjuku, and one of the world's best known bars. Owner Hiroyasu Kayama grows herbs on his family farm and grinds them for drinks in a mortar. There is no menu: say what you like and he makes it.
benfiddich.t: Mon to Sat 18:00 to 02:00, closed Sunday. Cover charge. Walk-in on a Monday is usually fine; booking helps at weekends. Pricey.

ny-bar.l: ニューヨーク バー
ny-bar.w: The jazz bar on the 52nd floor of the Park Hyatt, made famous by Lost in Translation. It reopened in December 2025 after the hotel's renovation. Floor to ceiling windows over the whole city, live jazz in the evening and classic cocktails.
ny-bar.t: Mon to Wed 17:00 to midnight, Thu to Sat to 01:00, Sun to 23:00. A music charge applies after 20:00. Smart casual enforced. Book for a window seat.
ny-bar.m: New York Bar Park Hyatt Tokyo

tocho-mapping.w: A free projection mapping show played across the whole east face of the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building. Each show runs about ten minutes, with music, and you watch from the plaza below.
tocho-mapping.t: Free, no tickets. October shows at 18:00, 18:30, 19:00, 19:30, 20:00, 20:30 and 21:30. Cancelled in storms. Ten minutes' walk from the west exit.
tocho-mapping.m: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Citizens Plaza

beams-japan.l: ビームス ジャパン 新宿
beams-japan.w: Five floors of the best of Japanese making, curated by the Beams fashion group. Souvenirs and craft on the ground floor, Japanese denim and labels upstairs, and the Fennica floor of folk craft, ceramics and furniture.

shin-okubo.w: Tokyo's Koreatown, one stop north of Shinjuku. Streets of K-pop shops, Korean skincare, street food stalls (cheese corn dogs, hotteok, tteokbokki) and fried chicken and pork belly restaurants.
shin-okubo.t: Shops mostly open 10:00 to 11:00. Weekday mornings are quietest, weekend afternoons packed. JR Yamanote one stop from Shinjuku, or a 15 minute walk.

thermae-yu.w: A large, modern hot spring bath in Kabukichō with six indoor baths and an open-air one, separate for men and women. A rare onsen in the city that lets tattooed visitors in, covered.
thermae-yu.t: Open 24 hours. Mon to Thu ¥2,700 (¥2,200 online), plus a late night surcharge. Foreign visitors show a passport. Tattoos must be covered; cover patches sold at the desk.

new-grand-cafe.l: ホテルニューグランド ザ・カフェ
new-grand-cafe.w: The coffee house of Yokohama's grand 1927 hotel, facing Yamashita Park. This is where spaghetti Napolitan, seafood doria and pudding à la mode were invented for post-war guests, and all three are still on the menu in a dining room that has barely changed.
new-grand-cafe.t: 10:00 to 21:30, last orders 21:00. Walk-in. Hotel prices, but a casual room.
new-grand-cafe.m: Hotel New Grand The Cafe Yokohama

edosei.l: 江戸清 中華街本店
edosei.w: Chinatown's famous pork bun shop. The signature nikuman is huge, about twice the size of a convenience store bun, with around ten other fillings including prawn chilli and braised pork belly. Eat it hot on the street.
edosei.t: Weekdays 10:00 to 19:30, Sat to 21:00, Sun to 20:30. Open daily. About ¥1,000 for a couple of buns. Walk-in, takeaway.

jukeihanten.w: A long running Sichuan restaurant in Chinatown, known for its mapo tofu made with long aged chilli bean paste. Also a Sichuan hot pot with two broths. A proper sit-down meal without the banquet formality.
jukeihanten.t: Weekdays 11:30 to 15:00 and 17:00 to 21:00 (last orders 20:00), Fri to 22:00. Open daily. Dinner about ¥6,000 to ¥12,000 a head.

manchinro.w: One of Chinatown's grand old Cantonese restaurants, dating from the 1890s. Banquet courses run from prawns in mayonnaise sauce and Peking duck to braised shark fin and abalone, served at round tables in an ornate dining room.
manchinro.t: 11:00 to 22:00, last orders 21:30. Closed days irregular. Dinner courses ¥8,000, ¥11,000 and ¥18,000 a head plus 10% service, minimum two people. Book online through Savor Japan (English).

heichinro.w: Said to be the oldest Chinese restaurant in Japan, founded about 130 years ago on Chinatown's main street. Classic Cantonese cooking and well regarded dim sum, plus Peking duck that takes three days to prepare.
heichinro.t: Weekdays 11:00 to 15:00 and 17:00 to 22:00, last orders 21:00. Closed days vary. Dinner from about ¥10,000 a head.

hammerhead.w: A pier building next to the old Hammerhead crane on the Minato Mirai waterfront, with more than 20 restaurants and food shops, many with open kitchens where you watch the food being made.
hammerhead.t: Daily about 11:00 to 23:00, shops vary. Walk-in. About 12 minutes' walk from the Red Brick Warehouses.

sea-guardian.w: The British style bar of the Hotel New Grand, all dark wood and leather, opposite Yamashita Park. A classic hotel bar for a proper cocktail before dinner in Chinatown, five minutes away.
sea-guardian.m: Bar Sea Guardian II Hotel New Grand

sirius.w: The lounge on the 70th floor of the Yokohama Royal Park Hotel, at the top of the Landmark Tower. Cocktails, a pianist at night and a view straight down over the harbour, the Ferris wheel and the Bay Bridge.
sirius.t: Evenings 17:30 to 22:30, drinks last orders 21:30. Book a window table online on the hotel site. Open daily.
sirius.m: Sky Lounge Sirius Yokohama Royal Park Hotel

osanbashi.w: The rooftop of Yokohama's cruise terminal, a rolling timber deck shaped like waves that juts into the harbour. It gives the best free view of the Minato Mirai skyline, the Ferris wheel and the Bay Bridge, and is lovely at dusk.
osanbashi.t: Free and open 24 hours. Ten minutes' walk from Yamashita Park.
osanbashi.m: Osanbashi Yokohama International Passenger Terminal rooftop

sky-garden.w: The observation deck on the 69th floor of the Landmark Tower, 273 metres up. A 360 degree view of the port and Minato Mirai, and Mount Fuji and Tokyo's towers on a clear day.
sky-garden.t: Weekdays 10:00 to 21:00, last entry 20:30. ¥1,000. Next to Sakuragichō Station.

marine-tower.w: A 1961 lattice tower at the end of Yamashita Park, refurbished in 2022, with a deck 94 metres up looking back at the Minato Mirai skyline and the Bay Bridge. Lower and more intimate than the Landmark Tower.
marine-tower.t: 10:00 to 22:00. Weekday day ticket ¥1,000, night ticket (from 18:00) ¥1,200, cheaper online. One minute from Motomachi-Chūkagai Station, exit 4.

yamate.n: Yamate Bluff and Harbor View Park
yamate.l: 山手 港の見える丘公園
yamate.w: The hill above Chinatown where foreign merchants built their homes after the port opened in 1859. A quiet walk past Western houses, the foreigners' cemetery and Harbor View Park, which looks out over the port to the Bay Bridge.
yamate.t: Western houses free, 09:30 to 17:00, each closed one Wednesday a month. Park always open. Uphill from Motomachi-Chūkagai Station.

motomachi.w: A tidy, old fashioned shopping street at the foot of the Bluff, which grew up serving the foreign residents of Yamate. Boutiques, bakeries, leather and homewares, and the birthplace of the late 1970s 'Hamatora' style.
motomachi.t: Shop hours vary. Next to Motomachi-Chūkagai Station, two minutes from Chinatown.

arabica-arashiyama.w: A tiny white coffee bar on the river just upstream from Togetsukyō bridge, with a glass front looking straight at the hills. The latte is the order. There is almost no seating, so take the cup down to the riverbank.
arabica-arashiyama.t: Daily, opens 08:00 or 09:00 depending on the season, to 18:00. Walk-in only. The queue builds through the morning. About ¥600 to ¥800 a coffee.

excafe.l: eX cafe 京都嵐山本店
excafe.w: A café in an old Arashiyama house with tatami rooms looking onto a garden. Known for warabi mochi you toast yourself over a small charcoal grill, and for matcha sets with Japanese sweets. A sit-down stop rather than a takeaway.
excafe.t: Opens about 10:00, closes late afternoon. Hours not confirmed for 2026, check Google Maps. Walk-in, expect a short wait. About ¥1,200 to ¥2,000 a head.

yudofu-sagano.w: A long running tofu restaurant near Tenryū-ji, in a house with a garden. The set is yudofu, silky tofu simmered at the table in a light kelp broth, with tempura, sesame tofu and rice alongside. Gentle, warming and very Kyoto.
yudofu-sagano.t: Lunch from about 11:00. Sets from about ¥3,800. Walk-in. Opening hours not confirmed for 2026, check Google Maps.

izakaya-ponto.l: 京都居酒屋 ぽんと
izakaya-ponto.w: A relaxed izakaya on the Pontochō alley serving Kyoto dishes: obanzai, yuba, fu dengaku, pickles, Saikyō-grilled fish and yakitori. Small plates from about ¥500, so you can graze and keep it casual.
izakaya-ponto.t: 16:00 to 22:00, last orders 21:00. Open daily with some irregular closures. About ¥4,500 a head. ¥660 seat charge on à la carte orders. Walk in, or have the hotel phone ahead (075-221-1537).

chao-chao.l: 餃子 ChaoChao 三条木屋町
chao-chao.w: A small, noisy gyoza bar on Kiyamachi, famous well beyond Kyoto for its crisp pan-fried dumplings. Try the classic, plus cheese, shrimp and the 18 cm stick gyoza. Cheap, fast and very good with a beer.
chao-chao.t: Mon to Thu 17:00 to 02:00, Fri 17:00 to 03:00, Sat 14:00 to 03:00, Sun 14:00 to 02:00. No bookings, queue at peak. About ¥1,000 to ¥2,000 a head.

menami.w: A Kiyamachi obanzai restaurant open since 1939, with a long counter lined with platters of Kyoto home cooking. Point at what looks good: simmered ebi-imo taro, yuba, braised vegetables, grilled fish. Listed with a Michelin Bib Gourmand.
menami.t: 15:00 to 21:30. Closed Wednesdays. About ¥3,000 to ¥8,000 a head. Walk-ins are easiest right at opening, it is often full by 19:00.

daiichi-asahi.l: 本家 第一旭 たかばし本店
daiichi-asahi.w: The classic Kyoto ramen shop, five minutes from Kyoto Station. A clear soy and pork broth, thin noodles, slices of chashu and a heap of Kujō green onion. No frills, quick turnover and a line out the door.
daiichi-asahi.t: 06:00 to 01:00. Closed Thursdays. Walk-in, buy a ticket and queue. About ¥1,000 a bowl.
daiichi-asahi.m: Honke Daiichi Asahi Takabashi Honten Kyoto

kagizen.l: 鍵善良房 四条本店
kagizen.w: A Gion sweet maker on Shijō-dōri, open since the Edo period, with a quiet tea room behind the shop. The thing to order is kuzukiri: cold, clear arrowroot noodles dipped in black sugar syrup, with a bowl of matcha.
kagizen.t: About 09:30 to 18:00, closed Mondays (confirm on Google Maps). Walk-in. Kuzukiri about ¥1,300.

endo-yasaka.l: 京都祇園 天ぷら 八坂圓堂
endo-yasaka.w: Course tempura in a wooden teahouse just south of Gion, a few minutes from the Yasaka Pagoda. Each piece comes straight from the oil at the counter: Kyoto vegetables, seasonal fish, and the famous sweetcorn tempura. About two hours.
endo-yasaka.t: Dinner 17:00 to 21:30, last orders 20:30. Open every day. Rokuhara course ¥16,000, Yasaka course ¥22,000, plus 13% service at the counter. Book in English on TableCheck.

gion-nakatani.w: A small kaiseki restaurant on the Shimbashi lanes beside the Shirakawa canal, in the prettiest part of Gion. A seasonal multi-course Kyoto dinner at a gentle price for the area, about 10 courses of small dishes.
gion-nakatani.t: Dinner 18:00 to 21:00. Closed Sundays. Dinner course about ¥10,000 to ¥11,000. Book online in English through Gurunavi or Savor Japan.

matsumuro.w: A quiet Japanese restaurant on Furumonzen-dōri, the antiques street at the north edge of Gion. Seasonal Kyoto cooking served as a dinner course, a step up from Nakatani in price.
matsumuro.t: Dinner 17:00 to 21:00. Irregular closures. About ¥15,000 to ¥20,000 a head. Book online in English through Savor Japan.

bees-knees.w: A speakeasy behind a bookshelf door, with 1990s hip-hop and inventive cocktails. It has been on Asia's 50 Best Bars list every year since 2020, peaking at number 18. Order the Ninja Smash.
bees-knees.t: 18:00 to about 01:00 or later. Closed Sundays. Walk-in, counter and a few seats. Mid priced cocktails.

escamoteur.w: A magician-themed cocktail bar a few doors from Kiyamachi, dark and theatrical, with swinging seats at the window. The bartenders are serious about spirits and playful about the drinks.
escamoteur.t: About 20:00 to 02:00. Check their Instagram (escamoteurbar) for closures. Walk-ins welcome. About ¥4,000 to ¥7,000 a head.

yoramu.w: A tiny sake bar off Nijō-dōri run by an Israeli sake obsessive. He pours tasting flights of small brewery sake, including aged sake, and explains each one in English.
yoramu.t: Evenings only, open a few nights a week. Days not confirmed for 2026, check Google Maps before going. Tasting flights about ¥1,500 to ¥2,000. Walk-in, small.

k36.w: The rooftop bar of The Hotel Seiryu Kyoto Kiyomizu, beside Yasaka Pagoda. From the roof you look across the temple roofs at the pagoda and over the city. Cocktails and wine, with a dim bar downstairs for colder nights.
k36.t: About 15:00 to midnight. Rooftop may close in bad weather. Walk-in for the rooftop. Hotel bar prices.
k36.m: K36 The Bar Rooftop Hotel Seiryu Kyoto Kiyomizu

kenninji.w: Kyoto's oldest Zen temple, founded in 1202, tucked behind the teahouses of Gion. Inside: a huge painting of twin dragons across the hall ceiling, a famous folding screen of the wind and thunder gods, and raked gravel gardens you can sit beside.
kenninji.t: About 10:00 to 17:00, last entry 16:30. About ¥800. Occasionally closed for ceremonies.

nanzenji.w: A big Zen temple at the south end of the Philosopher's Path, with a massive wooden gate you can climb and a red brick 19th century aqueduct running through the grounds. The grounds and the aqueduct are free.
nanzenji.t: Grounds free and open all day. The gate and the Hōjō garden have small fees and close about 17:00.

higashi-honganji.w: A vast temple on Karasuma-dōri, between Kyoto Station and your hotel. Its Founder's Hall is one of the largest wooden buildings in the world, and you can walk in, sit on the tatami and look up. Free and rarely crowded.
higashi-honganji.t: Free. About 05:50 to 17:30 from March to October. Shoes off inside the halls.

uji.w: A small riverside town 20 minutes south of Kyoto that has grown Japan's finest green tea for 800 years. Byōdō-in, the Phoenix Hall on the ¥10 coin, sits beside the river, and the street to it is lined with tea houses serving matcha and matcha sweets.
uji.t: JR Nara line from Kyoto Station, about 20 minutes, Suica. Byōdō-in about 08:30 to 17:30. Allow half a day.

fushimi-sake.w: The old brewing quarter of Fushimi, south of the shrine, where soft spring water made Kyoto famous for sake. Black timber warehouses line a willow canal. The Gekkeikan Ōkura Sake Museum runs a tasting at the end of its small museum.
fushimi-sake.t: Chūshojima station on the Keihan line, two stops from Fushimi-Inari. Gekkeikan museum about 09:30 to 16:30, entry about ¥600 including a tasting. Confirm hours before going.

mentoan.w: A tiny udon shop in Naramachi, known for kinchaku kitsune udon: a whole fried tofu pouch tied like a drawstring bag, with udon hidden inside, in a light dashi. Quick, cheap and very Nara.
mentoan.t: Lunchtime, with a closed day or two each week. Hours not confirmed for 2026, check Google Maps. Walk-in. About ¥1,000 to ¥1,500.

mizuya-chaya.w: A thatched roof teahouse in the woods on the path between Kasuga Taisha and Tōdai-ji, beside a small stream. Matcha, mochi, shaved ice in the warm months and simple udon, at outdoor benches under the trees.
mizuya-chaya.t: Daytime only, closes late afternoon. Irregular closures. Hours not confirmed for 2026. Cash is safest.

harushika.l: 春鹿 今西清兵衛商店
harushika.w: A working sake brewery in Naramachi, in the family since 1884. At the shop counter you pay a small fee to taste five sakes poured by the staff, and keep the glass. Nara claims to be the birthplace of refined sake.
harushika.t: Daytime tasting, roughly 10:00 to 17:00. Fee about ¥500 to ¥1,000. Confirm hours on Google Maps before going. Walk-in.

kokuhokan.w: The museum inside Kōfuku-ji's grounds, which you walk through on the way to the deer. It holds the temple's best statues, including Ashura, a slender three-faced, six-armed figure from 734 that is one of the most loved sculptures in Japan.
kokuhokan.t: About 09:00 to 17:00, last entry 16:45. Entry about ¥900. Open daily. No photos.

yoshikien.w: Three small gardens right next door to Isuien: a pond garden, a moss garden and a tea ceremony garden, around a former private house. Quieter than Isuien and usually free for overseas visitors who show a passport.
yoshikien.t: About 09:00 to 17:00, last entry 16:30. Free for overseas visitors with a passport. Check closed days before going.

naramachi.w: The old merchant quarter just south of Sanjō-dōri: narrow lanes of dark wooden townhouses with latticed fronts, now holding small cafés, craft shops, a sake brewery and sweet shops. A calm half hour away from the park crowds.
naramachi.t: Ten minutes' walk south of Kōfuku-ji. Many shops close around 17:00 and some on Mondays.

koshi-no-ie.w: A restored merchant's townhouse in Naramachi that you can walk through: the narrow street front, the tiny courtyard garden, the steep box staircase and the long earth-floored kitchen. A quick way to see how these houses work inside.

nakagawa-masashichi.w: The original shop of a Nara textile house founded in 1716, famous for fine Nara hand-woven linen. Today it sells beautifully designed tea towels, small cloth goods and homewares. Good small gifts.
nakagawa-masashichi.t: Daytime shop hours. Check Google Maps before going.

r-baker.l: R Baker 大阪城公園店
r-baker.w: A bakery café inside Osaka Castle Park, near the Morinomiya side, baking with Japanese rice flour so the bread has a soft, chewy bite. Curry bread, sausage rolls, the stretchy croissant and iced matcha lattes, all easy to carry to a bench by the moat.
r-baker.t: Weekdays 07:00 to 17:00, weekends to 18:00. Closed only over New Year. Most pastries about ¥200 to ¥300. Walk-in.
r-baker.m: R Baker Osaka Castle Park 3-9 Osakajo

horai-551.w: Osaka's beloved pork bun shop, with queues at every branch. The butaman is a big, soft steamed bun filled with juicy pork and onion, sold hot to eat on the spot or boxed to take home. Their shūmai and gyōza are good too.
horai-551.t: Many branches: the main shop is on Ebisubashi-suji, two minutes from Dōtonbori, and there are counters in Namba Walk and at Osaka and Shin-Osaka stations. The Namba Walk shop is 11:00 to 22:00, closed the third Wednesday. Hours vary by branch. A bun is a few hundred yen.

kurogin.w: The tuna specialist at Kuromon, cutting fat tuna, lean red tuna and seared belly in front of you. Order a sashimi plate or a tuna bowl and eat it at the counter inside. The best single stop in the market for fish.
kurogin.t: Daily 09:30 to 16:30. About ¥2,000 to ¥3,000 a head. Walk-in. Bring cash for the market in general.

kuromon-sanpei.w: A big seafood shop near the middle of Kuromon with its own eat-in area. Pick uni, oysters in the shell, sashimi or sushi from the counter, they prepare it, and you sit down to eat. Seafood bowls are eat-in only.
kuromon-sanpei.t: Daily 09:30 to 17:00. Walk-in. Prices by item, market rates.

daruma-shinsekai.l: 元祖串かつ だるま 新世界総本店
daruma-shinsekai.w: The original Daruma, open since 1929, under the angry chef statue a block from Tsūtenkaku. Skewers of beef, pork, prawn, lotus root and quail egg, fried in a light, crisp batter and dipped once in the shared sauce. No double dipping.
daruma-shinsekai.t: Daily 11:00 to 22:30. Skewers about ¥130 to ¥380, a snack plus a beer about ¥1,500 to ¥2,500. Cards and PayPay accepted. Walk-in, short queues at dusk.

tengu.w: A favourite kushikatsu counter inside Janjan-Yokochō, under the long-nosed red demon above the door. Cheap, consistently good skewers and doteyaki, beef tendon stewed in sweet miso. Locals queue for it.
tengu.t: 10:30 to 20:00 or so, closed Mondays. Skewers about ¥100 to ¥200, fried prawn about ¥450. Walk-in, no bookings.

wanaka.l: たこ焼道楽 わなか 千日前本店
wanaka.w: The takoyaki shop locals name first. A dashi-rich batter cooked in copper pans so the shell is crisp and the inside molten. Try the plain sauce first, or the OOIRI set of four flavours. Seats upstairs.
wanaka.t: Weekdays 10:00 to 23:00, weekends from 08:30. Open all year. Eight pieces about ¥600 to ¥850. Walk-in.

mizuno.w: A family-run okonomiyaki shop on Dōtonbori since 1945, cooked for you on the griddle at your seat. The Mizuno-yaki uses a yam batter, and the mixed seafood and pork is the classic. A long queue moves fast, and staff take your order while you wait.
mizuno.t: 11:00 to 22:00, last orders 21:00. Closed days unclear: one listing says closed Thursdays, others say open daily. Check Google Maps on the day. From about ¥1,500. No bookings.

fukutaro.w: A loud, cheerful Sennichimae okonomiyaki house famous for negiyaki: a thin batter packed with green spring onion, cooked with beef tendon or pork and finished with soy and lemon instead of the sweet sauce. Their okonomiyaki is excellent too.
fukutaro.t: Mon to Fri 17:00 to 00:30, Sat, Sun and holidays 12:00 to 23:30. Open daily. About ¥2,000 a head. No bookings: write your name on the list inside and wait to be called.

imai.l: 道頓堀 今井 本店
imai.w: An old udon house in a quiet wooden front on the busiest street in Osaka, known for its delicate dashi. The kitsune udon is the order: soft noodles in clear broth topped with sweet simmered fried tofu. A calm sit-down in the middle of the neon.
imai.t: 11:30 to 20:30, last orders 20:00. Closed Wednesdays, so Thursday is fine. Lunch about ¥1,500, dinner about ¥2,000. Walk-in.

kani-doraku.l: かに道楽 道頓堀本店
kani-doraku.w: The restaurant under Dōtonbori's giant moving crab sign, serving nothing but crab: crab hot pot, sashimi, grilled legs, tempura and sushi, as set courses in private-feeling tatami rooms. Touristy, but a genuinely good crab feast and very Osaka.
kani-doraku.t: 11:00 to 23:00, last entry 22:00. Dinner about ¥8,000 a head. Book online in English through Gurunavi. Cards accepted. English tablet menu.

rikuro.l: りくろーおじさんの店 なんば本店
rikuro.w: Osaka's wobbly, fluffy Japanese cheesecake, baked all day with raisins on the base and branded with the old man's face. When a fresh batch comes out the staff ring a bell. Light enough to eat a slice warm on the street.
rikuro.t: Shop 09:00 to 20:00, closed 1 January only. Café upstairs 11:30 to 17:30. A whole 18 cm cake is ¥965. Walk-in, queues are quick.
rikuro.m: Rikuro Ojisan no Mise Namba Honten

matsubaya.w: The shop that claims to have invented kitsune udon in 1893, by putting sweet fried tofu on udon. Still a modest, family-run room. The other famous dish is ojiya udon, udon and rice in a little iron pot with egg and seafood.
matsubaya.t: 11:00 to 18:00. Closed Sundays and public holidays. Inexpensive. Walk-in. Five minutes from Shinsaibashi station.

meoto-zenzai.w: A sweet shop founded in 1883 beside the mossy Mizukake Fudō. The one dish is zenzai, sweet red bean soup with mochi, served as two small bowls for a couple, which is said to bring a happy marriage.

craftroom.w: A tiny cocktail bar two floors underground in an old Umeda office block full of izakaya, run by Ryu Fujii, a former World Class runner-up. It was the first Osaka bar on Asia's 50 Best Bars list, and is No. 58 on the 2025 extended list. About ten seats.
craftroom.t: 16:00 to midnight. Closed Sundays. Walk-in, wait if full. Ekimae Daiichi Building B2, five minutes from Osaka Station.
craftroom.m: CRAFTROOM Osaka Ekimae Daiichi Building B2

bar-nayuta.w: A hidden fifth floor bar opposite Triangle Park in Amerikamura, marked only by a geometric symbol. There is no menu: tell the bartender what you like and they build a drink from house infusions, bitters and liqueurs. No. 100 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025 extended list.

bar36.l: Bar36 スイスホテル南海大阪
bar36.w: The hotel's 36th floor bar, 147 metres up, sitting directly on top of Namba Station. Big windows over the neon of Minami and the city skyline, with cocktails and live music on weekends.
bar36.t: Sun to Thu 15:00 to 23:30, last orders 22:45. Walk-in, or book by email (Bar36.Osaka@swissotel.com) or WhatsApp. Hotel bar prices.

mizukake-chaya.l: 法善寺横丁 炉端焼 水掛茶屋
mizukake-chaya.w: A relaxed robatayaki izakaya right in Hōzenji Yokochō, with a counter in front of the grill and small rooms behind. Sake, a beer and a few grilled skewers or fish, in the quiet lane after the noise of Dōtonbori. English menu.
mizukake-chaya.t: 16:00 to 23:00. Closed only over New Year. Dishes from about ¥300. Walk-in for two is usually fine on a weeknight.

shitennoji.w: One of Japan's oldest temples, founded in 593 by Prince Shōtoku, with a five storey pagoda and a large stone-paved precinct. On the 21st and 22nd of every month the outer grounds fill with a flea market of several hundred stalls: old kimono, pottery, records, toys and food stalls.
shitennoji.t: Outer grounds open all day and free. Central precinct 08:30 to 16:00 in October, ¥300. Flea market 08:30 to sunset on the 21st and 22nd, cash only, cancelled in bad weather.

doguyasuji.l: 千日前道具屋筋商店街
doguyasuji.w: A 150 metre covered street of shops for the restaurant trade, between Namba and Kuromon. Japanese knives, takoyaki pans, lacquer, noren curtains and the plastic food models you see in restaurant windows. Some shops run food sample making workshops.
doguyasuji.t: Hours vary by shop, roughly 10:00 to 18:00. Three minutes from Namba Station.

pokemon-osaka.l: ポケモンセンターオーサカDX・Nintendo OSAKA
pokemon-osaka.w: The Pokémon Center Osaka DX and Nintendo's official Osaka store share the 13th floor of Daimaru Umeda, above Osaka Station. Exclusive Mario, Zelda and Pokémon merchandise, and some designs only sold here and in Tokyo.
pokemon-osaka.t: 10:00 to 20:00 (Daimaru hours, Nintendo listed to 21:00 in some sources). Open daily. Free entry.
pokemon-osaka.m: Daimaru Umeda 13F Pokemon Center Nintendo Osaka

ura-namba.w: Back Namba: the grid of small streets east of Namba Station packed with tiny izakaya, standing bars and wine bars. Torame Yokochō, an alley with a red torii and nine little venues sharing seats, is an easy way in.
ura-namba.t: Mostly evenings from about 17:00. Venues vary, some cash only. Walk-in.

sumiyoshi.w: The head shrine of some 2,000 Sumiyoshi shrines across Japan, older than Buddhism's arrival in Osaka. The steep red arched Sorihashi bridge is the photo, and the halls are in a plain, ancient style found almost nowhere else.
sumiyoshi.t: October 06:30 to 17:00. Free. Nankai Main Line local train from Namba, four stops, about 10 minutes and ¥240.

tsumugi.l: 築地本願寺カフェ Tsumugi
tsumugi.w: A bright café in the grounds of Tsukiji Hongwanji, the Indian-style temple beside the old market. The famous order is the 18-dish breakfast: rice porridge, miso soup and 16 tiny seasonal dishes such as tamagoyaki, duck with sanshō pepper and matcha jelly.
tsumugi.t: Café 08:00 to 17:00, breakfast to 10:30. 18-dish breakfast about ¥2,200 (¥1,800 in older listings), only about 50 a day at weekends. No bookings: weekend waits of 20 to 30 minutes.

arabica-azabudai.w: The Kyoto-born coffee chain's Azabudai Hills café, in the basement of Garden Plaza right by Kamiyachō Station. Good espresso and a Spanish latte, with pastries.
arabica-azabudai.m: % Arabica Azabudai Hills Garden Plaza B1

kimuraya.w: The bakery that invented anpan, the soft bun filled with sweet red bean paste, in 1874. The classic is the sakadane anpan made with sake yeast and topped with a salted cherry blossom. A café on 2F does light meals and cakes.
kimuraya.t: 1F bakery and 2F café 10:00 to 20:00 (café last orders 19:00). Closed 31 Dec and 1 Jan. Anpan about ¥200 to ¥300 each.

bairin.w: Ginza's oldest tonkatsu house, open since 1927, in a basement in Ginza 7-chōme. Kagoshima black pork cutlets with free refills of rice, a good katsudon, and a hirekatsu (fillet) sando you can also take away.
bairin.t: 11:30 to 21:00, last orders 20:00. Closed New Year only. No bookings. About ¥1,200 to ¥5,000. Cards accepted.

tsunahachi-matsuya.l: 新宿つな八 銀座松屋店
tsunahachi-matsuya.w: A branch of the much-loved Shinjuku tempura house on Matsuya's 8F restaurant floor. Prawns, fish and vegetables fried in sesame oil and served in sets or as tendon, with an English menu and no fuss.
tsunahachi-matsuya.t: Daily 11:00 to 22:00, last orders 21:00. Lunch about ¥2,000, dinner about ¥4,500. Walk-in.

lion.l: ビヤホールライオン 銀座七丁目店
lion.w: Japan's oldest surviving beer hall, opened by Sapporo in 1934 and now a registered cultural property. A grand, mosaic-walled hall serving Sapporo draught with German-leaning bar food: sausages, schnitzel, karaage.
lion.t: 11:30 to 23:00, Sundays and holidays to 22:30. Walk-in. Dinner from about ¥2,500 a head with beer.

kondo.l: もんじゃ 近どう 本店
kondo.w: The best-known shop on Tsukishima's Monja Street, dozens of monjayaki places along one road. Monjayaki is Tokyo's own runny, cheesy cousin of okonomiyaki: you fry it on the hotplate at your table and scrape it off with tiny spatulas. Staff will show you how.
kondo.t: Mon to Fri 17:00 to 22:00. Sat, Sun and holidays 11:30 to 22:00. Last orders 21:30. About ¥2,500 a head at dinner. Cards accepted. Walk-in, queues at weekends.

yamanoue.l: てんぷら 山の上 銀座
yamanoue.w: The Ginza branch of the tempura counter from the old Hilltop Hotel, on the 13th floor of Ginza Six. You sit at the counter while the chef fries each piece and hands it straight over: prawns, seasonal fish, ginkgo nuts, sweet potato, lotus root.
yamanoue.t: Lunch 11:00 to 15:00, dinner 17:00 to 23:30 (last orders 20:30). Lunch course about ¥16,000 at last review, dinner roughly ¥20,000 to ¥28,000 a head. Book in English on TableCheck.

daikokuya.w: An Asakusa institution since 1887 for tendon, a bowl of rice under big prawn tempura soaked in a dark, sweet and salty sauce. Fried in sesame oil, rich and very filling.
daikokuya.t: 11:00 to 20:00, no regular closing day. Tendon from about ¥1,700. Cash only. No bookings, expect a queue at noon.

asakusa-menchi.w: A takeaway counter near Sensō-ji selling one thing: menchi katsu, a crumbed, deep-fried patty of minced pork and beef, juicy and hot from the fryer. Eat it standing outside.

uokin.w: The original of a popular Shimbashi seafood izakaya chain, a minute from the station. Generous sashimi platters, grilled fish and cold beer, in a cramped, cheerful room full of office workers.
uokin.t: Mon to Fri 15:00 to 23:00, Sat, Sun and holidays 13:00 to 23:00. Food last orders 22:15. Walk-in, short queue at 19:00 likely. English menu or English-speaking staff.

tonton.w: A smoky yakitori and pork-skewer joint built into the brick arches under the JR tracks at Yūrakuchō, with stools spilling onto the lane. The kashira (pork cheek) skewer is the house specialty, with chicken, heart, liver and miso-glazed eggplant.
tonton.t: 11:30 to 23:00 daily at last report (check Google Maps). Skewers from about ¥200. English menu. Walk-in, cash.

bar-high-five.l: バー ハイファイブ
bar-high-five.w: Hidetsugu Ueno's basement bar in Ginza 5-chōme, once No. 3 on the World's 50 Best Bars and still one of the most respected in Asia. There is no menu: tell the bartender what you like and they make it. Famous for hard-shaken classics and hand-cut ice.
bar-high-five.t: Mon to Sat from 17:00. Closed Sundays and national holidays. ¥1,000 cover including snacks. Walk-in, arrive early for the counter, or reserve via the bar's website.
bar-high-five.m: Bar High Five Efflore Ginza5 B1F 5-4-15 Ginza

star-bar.l: スタア・バー・ギンザ
star-bar.w: Hisashi Kishi's classic Ginza cocktail bar, a quiet, wood-panelled basement where the sidecar is the drink to order. Precise, formal Japanese bartending at its most refined.
star-bar.t: 17:00 to 24:00, last orders 23:30. Closed Mondays and every other Tuesday. ¥1,000 cover. Phone bookings, or walk in early.

peter-bar.w: The bar on the 24th floor of The Peninsula Tokyo, ten minutes' walk from your hotel. Big windows look over Hibiya Park and the Imperial Palace gardens, with Japanese whiskies, Champagne and signature cocktails.
peter-bar.t: Mon to Thu 17:00 to 23:00, Fri 17:00 to 24:00, Sat 15:00 to 24:00, Sun and holidays 15:00 to 22:00. Signature Tokyo Joe ¥2,600. Walk-in, or call 03 6270 2888.
peter-bar.m: Peter the Bar The Peninsula Tokyo 24F

caretta.l: カレッタ汐留 SKY VIEW
caretta.w: A free viewing area on the 46th floor of the Caretta Shiodome tower, about 200 metres up, five minutes' walk from the hotel. It looks out over Hama-rikyū gardens, Tsukiji, Tokyo Bay and Rainbow Bridge, best after dark.
caretta.t: Free. 11:00 to 23:00. Closed 1 and 2 January. Take the direct lift from B2.

hamarikyu.w: A former shōgun's duck-hunting garden on the edge of Tokyo Bay, with a seawater tidal pond and the Shiodome towers rising behind it. The Nakajima teahouse sits on the pond and serves whisked matcha with a sweet.
hamarikyu.t: Daily 09:00 to 17:00, last entry 16:30. ¥300. Teahouse 09:00 to 16:45, matcha and wagashi ¥1,000. Cash or card.

kuramae.l: 蔵前 ダンデライオン・チョコレート
kuramae.w: Kuramae is a quiet former warehouse district just south of Asakusa, now known for small makers' shops and cafés. Dandelion Chocolate's factory café is the anchor: bean to bar chocolate, a brownie flight and a hot chocolate made with local green tea.
kuramae.t: Dandelion Chocolate daily 10:00 to 19:00. About 15 minutes' walk south of Kappabashi, or Kuramae Station on the Asakusa line.

konbini.w: Japan's convenience stores are a food destination. The three to try: 7-Eleven's tamago sando (soft egg salad sandwich), FamilyMart's Famichiki (juicy fried chicken from the hot case) and Lawson's Karaage-kun nuggets, plus onigiri with salmon or tuna mayo.
konbini.t: Open 24 hours, everywhere. Snacks ¥150 to ¥300. Cards and Suica.

depachika.w: The basement food halls of the big department stores: immaculate counters of bento, sushi, tempura, wagashi, cakes, fruit and pickles. Ginza Mitsukoshi, Matsuya and the B2 floor of Ginza Six are the best near your hotel. Good for a picnic dinner or gifts.
depachika.t: Roughly 10:00 to 20:00 (Ginza Six 10:30 to 20:30). In the last hour many counters mark down bento and sushi.

nakamura-tokichi.w: The Ginza café of a Uji tea merchant founded in 1859, on 4F of Ginza Six. Proper matcha in parfaits, jellies and ice cream, plus thin green-tea soba if you want a light meal.
nakamura-tokichi.t: 10:30 to 20:30, last orders 19:30. No regular closing day. About ¥1,500 to ¥2,000. Walk-in, queue at weekends.

toraya.w: The flagship Ginza shop and tea room of Toraya, the wagashi maker that has supplied the imperial court for about five centuries. Known for yōkan (sweet bean jelly) and seasonal sweets, served with matcha upstairs.
toraya.t: 11:00 to 19:00, last orders 18:30. Closed 1 January and the 2nd Monday of each month (in October 2026 that falls on 19 October because of the holiday). Counter seats need a booking.

hasegawa.l: はせがわ酒店 グランスタ東京店
hasegawa.w: A respected sake shop with a tasting bar inside Tokyo Station. Order a glass or a flight of small pours from breweries all over Japan, then buy a bottle of the one you liked.
hasegawa.t: Mon to Sat 07:00 to 22:00, Sun and holidays 07:00 to 21:00. Inside the JR ticket gates, B1 GranSta. From outside you need a JR platform ticket (about ¥150).

konparu-yu.w: A family-run neighbourhood sento (public bath) in Ginza 8-chōme, in business since 1863, five minutes from the hotel. Hot baths, tiled Mt Fuji murals and an old-Tokyo atmosphere, amid the designer stores.
konparu-yu.t: 14:00 to 22:00, Saturday to 20:00. Closed Sundays and public holidays. ¥600 cash. Bring a small towel and soap or buy them at the counter. Separate men's and women's baths.

laqua.w: A big, modern hot spring spa at Tokyo Dome City, fed by natural onsen water. Indoor and open-air baths, saunas and lounges, with towels and loungewear included. The easiest proper onsen in central Tokyo.
laqua.t: 11:00 to 09:00 next morning. From ¥3,500 (varies by day), ¥1,000 less if you enter after 19:00. No tattoos. Closed 5 to 9 October 2026 for maintenance (before you arrive).

karaoke-kan.l: カラオケ館 渋谷本店
karaoke-kan.w: The Shibuya karaoke building where Bill Murray and Scarlett Johansson sang in Lost in Translation. You hire a private room by the hour, order drinks by phone, and sing from a huge English catalogue.
karaoke-kan.t: Rates vary by time of day and room, with all-you-can-drink plans. Rooms 601 and 602 were the film rooms, ask at the desk. Phone 03 3462 0785.

purikura.w: A floor of purikura booths, the Japanese photo stickers where the machine smooths your skin, enlarges your eyes and lets you scribble on the results. Silly, very Japanese, and a fun souvenir for two.
purikura.t: Open 24 hours. About ¥400 to ¥500 a session, coins or Suica on newer machines. Men are often not allowed in without a woman in the group, so go together. 3F, 29-1 Udagawachō, beside the Swatch store.

gachapon.w: Walls of coin-operated capsule toy machines with tiny, oddly specific collectables: miniature food, anime figures, animals in hats. #C-pla on Center-gai in Shibuya has over 2,000 machines; #C-pla premium in Marronnier Gate Ginza 1 has 1,000, with pricier, nicer capsules.
gachapon.t: #C-pla Shibuya 10:00 to 23:00. #C-pla premium Ginza, Marronnier Gate 1 4F, 11:00 to 21:00. Bandai's official shop in Tokyo Station's Character Street, B1, 10:00 to 20:30. ¥300 to ¥500 a go, coins.

uniqlo-ginza.w: Uniqlo's global flagship and its biggest store in Japan: twelve floors on Chūō-dōri and a corner for customising tote bags.

daiso-ginza.l: ダイソー マロニエゲート銀座店
daiso-ginza.w: The flagship of Japan's biggest 100 yen chain: about 23,000 items, from snacks and kitchen gadgets to souvenirs, with sister shops Standard Products (smart homewares) and Threeppy (mostly ¥300) on the same floor.

loft-ginza.w: Five floors of clever Japanese lifestyle goods: stationery, pens and notebooks, beauty and skincare with a tester bar, kitchen gadgets and gift wrapping. The place for small, well-made souvenirs.
loft-ginza.t: 11:00 to 21:00 with the rest of Marronnier Gate Ginza 2. Tax-free with your passport.

bic-yurakucho.l: ビックカメラ 有楽町店
bic-yurakucho.w: A huge electronics store beside Yūrakuchō Station: cameras, headphones, Japanese gadgets, toys, and a drinks floor with a wide range of Japanese whisky and sake at fair prices.
bic-yurakucho.t: 10:00 to 22:00. Tax-free counter, bring your passport.

taxfree.w: Tourists can skip Japan's 10% consumption tax in shops showing the Tax-Free sign. On your dates the old system still applies: the tax comes off at the till. Spend at least ¥5,000 before tax in one store on one day, and show your physical passport.
taxfree.t: Consumables (food, cosmetics, alcohol) go into a sealed bag that must stay sealed until you leave Japan. From 1 November 2026 Japan switches to a refund at the airport instead, so this trip uses the simple old way.

hakone.w: Mountain hot spring country about 85 minutes from Shinjuku on the Odakyū Romancecar. A loop by train, cable car and ropeway takes in the volcanic vents at Ōwakudani, a pirate-ship cruise on Lake Ashi and, on a clear day, Mt Fuji.
hakone.t: A full day. The Hakone Freepass covers most of the loop. The Ōwakudani ropeway shuts when volcanic gas levels rise, so check on the day.

nikko.w: Mountain town two hours north of Asakusa on the Tōbu limited express, home to the lavishly gilded Tōshō-gū shrine in a forest of giant cedars. Higher up, Lake Chūzenji and Kegon Falls, where the autumn colour arrives in October, well before Tokyo.
nikko.t: A long full day. Tōbu trains leave from Asakusa. Shrines close about 16:00 to 17:00 in autumn.

man-wah.w: The Michelin starred Cantonese restaurant on the 25th floor of the Mandarin Oriental, freshly redesigned in dark blue and brass, with windows over the harbour. Classic Cantonese done with polish: Peking duck served two ways, barbecued Iberian pork with longan honey, lobster in a rich fish broth.
man-wah.t: Dinner nightly from 18:00 to about 22:30 (some listings say 18:30 to 22:00). From about HK$800 a head before drinks. Smart casual. Not on OpenTable: book on the Mandarin Oriental website or call +852 2825 4003. Cards accepted.
man-wah.m: Man Wah Mandarin Oriental Hong Kong 25F

mott32.w: A glamorous basement dining room under the Standard Chartered Bank building, famous for its apple wood roasted Peking duck. Also known for Iberico pork char siu and the soft quail egg siu mai. Big, dark and buzzy, and a proper night out.
mott32.t: Dinner 17:30 to midnight, lunch 11:30 to 14:30. About HK$1,000 a head. Book by phone +852 2885 8688 or on mott32.com, and pre-order the Peking duck and char siu when you book.
mott32.m: Mott 32 Standard Chartered Bank Building Des Voeux Road Central

ho-lee-fook.w: A loud, fun SoHo dining room with a wall of gold waving cats, mahjong tiles and 1980s Cantopop on the stereo. Creative Cantonese with real wok hei: kurobuta pork char siu, crispy three yellow chicken, steamed razor clams with glass noodles.
ho-lee-fook.t: Dinner only, 18:00 to 22:30 Sun to Wed, to 23:30 Thu to Sat. Cheaper than the other two, roughly HK$500 to 800 a head with drinks. Book online at holeefook.com.hk or +852 2810 0860. Ask about dishes that need pre-ordering.
ho-lee-fook.m: Ho Lee Fook 3-5 Elgin Street Central

hutong.w: A long running Northern Chinese restaurant high up in Tsim Sha Tsui, styled like an old Beijing courtyard house with red lanterns and carved screens. Known for the Red Lantern crispy soft shell crab buried in dried chillies and a flaming Peking duck.
hutong.t: Now on 18/F, H Zentre, 15 Middle Road, three minutes from the Sheraton. Daily 12:00 to midnight at last listing. Expensive, about HK$700 to 1,000 a head. Reservations essential: hutong.com.hk or +852 3428 8342.
hutong.m: Hutong H Zentre 15 Middle Road Tsim Sha Tsui

mak-man-kee.w: A Jordan noodle shop serving Hong Kong's classic wonton noodles: thin, springy egg noodles and plump prawn wontons in a clear, savoury broth, in a tiny bowl. Fast, cheap and a Michelin Bib Gourmand.
mak-man-kee.t: Daily 12:00 to 00:30. Under HK$100 a head. Walk-in. No credit cards, bring cash. 51 Parkes Street, Jordan, about 15 minutes' walk north of the hotel.
mak-man-kee.m: Mak Man Kee Noodle Shop 51 Parkes Street Jordan

yat-lok.w: A small, plain roast meat shop in Central with a Michelin star for its roast goose: crackling skin, juicy meat, sold by the quarter. Order it over lai fun rice noodles in clear broth with a little goose fat. The char siu is excellent too.
yat-lok.t: Daily 10:00 to 20:30. About HK$150 to 300 a head. Walk-in, expect a short queue and shared tables. 34-38 Stanley Street, Central.
yat-lok.m: Yat Lok Roast Goose 34 Stanley Street Central

lan-fong-yuen.w: A cramped old cha chaan teng and dai pai dong stall on Gage Street, said to be where Hong Kong milk tea was first strained through a silk stocking. Have the smooth, strong milk tea with a pork chop bun.
lan-fong-yuen.t: Mon to Sat 07:30 to 18:00, closed Sunday. Cheap. Walk-in, share tables, be quick. 2 Gage Street, at the bottom of Graham Street Market.
lan-fong-yuen.m: Lan Fong Yuen 2 Gage Street Central

bakehouse.w: The egg tart everyone in Hong Kong talks about now: a sourdough pastry shell, flaky and buttery, around a barely set custard, served warm. Good coffee too. For the 1950s classic with a short crust, Tai Cheong Bakery is two blocks away on Lyndhurst Terrace.
bakehouse.t: Daily 08:00 to 21:00. Egg tart HK$14, coffee about HK$45. SoHo shop at 5 Staunton Street is takeaway only, beside the Mid-Levels escalator. There is also a branch at 44 Hankow Road, TST, five minutes from the hotel.

hing-kee.w: The best known claypot rice on Temple Street. Rice is cooked in clay pots over a flame until a crisp crust forms at the bottom, topped with things like pork brisket, Chinese sausage or chicken, then finished with sweet soy. Also good: the crispy oyster omelette and fried squid. Four Seasons Pot Rice on Arthur Street is the charcoal fired rival, with queues from 18:00, and Temple Street Spicy Crabs at the Nanking Street corner does street-side typhoon shelter style seafood.
hing-kee.t: 15 Temple Street, Yau Ma Tei. Evenings 17:30 to midnight. Claypots about HK$50 to 100, around HK$100 to 150 a head. Cash only. Walk-in. Claypots take 20 minutes, so order first.
hing-kee.m: Hing Kee Restaurant 15 Temple Street Yau Ma Tei

maxims-city-hall.w: The classic big Hong Kong yum cha hall: a huge, noisy room with chandeliers and harbour views, where staff push steaming trolleys of dim sum between the tables and you point at what you want. Very popular, and the full old style experience.
maxims-city-hall.t: Dim sum by trolley Mon to Sat 11:00 to 15:00. About HK$200 to 300 a head. Call +852 2521 1303 to ask about a booking, otherwise expect to queue at lunch. 2/F, City Hall Low Block, five minutes' walk from the Central Star Ferry pier.

spring-moon.w: The Peninsula's Michelin starred Cantonese restaurant, all 1920s Art Deco wood panelling and stained glass. Refined, beautifully made dim sum at lunch, with a resident tea master. The calm, upscale way to do yum cha.
spring-moon.t: Lunch Mon to Sat 11:30 to 14:30, Sunday from 11:00. About HK$500 to 800 a head at lunch. Smart casual. Book on peninsula.com or call +852 2696 6760. Ten minutes' walk from the Sheraton.
spring-moon.m: Spring Moon The Peninsula Hong Kong

celestial-court.w: The Cantonese restaurant on the 2nd floor of your own hotel, Michelin listed and a favourite with local families. A recently refreshed dim sum list at lunch. No windows, but no travel and no queue on your last day.
celestial-court.t: Mon to Sat 11:30 to 15:00 and 18:00 to 22:00, Sunday from 10:30. Mid priced. Book online at celestialcourt.hk or call +852 2732 6991.
celestial-court.m: Celestial Court Sheraton Hong Kong Hotel

lei-garden-elements.w: One branch of a trusted Hong Kong Cantonese chain, in the Elements mall directly below Ozone. Good roast meats and crispy roast pork, steamed egg white with crab, and slow boiled soups. Reliable rather than flashy, and right where you need it.
lei-garden-elements.t: Shop 2068-70, 2/F, Water Zone, Elements. Lunch and dinner daily. A full dinner for two runs just over HK$500 a head without wine. Book by phone, +852 2196 8133.

mammy-pancake.w: A tiny takeaway counter making gai daan jai, the Hong Kong egg waffle: a sheet of crisp edged bubbles, soft and eggy inside, eaten hot from a paper bag. Michelin street food listed since 2016, with flavours from plain to chocolate chip and matcha.
mammy-pancake.t: 8-12 Carnarvon Road, TST, five minutes from the hotel. About HK$30 to 40. Walk-in, short queue. Hours run from around midday into the evening, check Google Maps.
mammy-pancake.m: Mammy Pancake 8-12 Carnarvon Road Tsim Sha Tsui

kam-wah.w: The famous home of bo lo yau: a hot pineapple bun, named for its crackly sugar top, split and stuffed with a thick slab of cold butter. Have it with milk tea and Hong Kong French toast in a busy old style cafe in Prince Edward.
kam-wah.t: Daily 06:30 to 23:30. Cheap, under HK$100 a head. Walk-in, expect a queue and shared tables. 47 Bute Street, Prince Edward.
kam-wah.m: Kam Wah Cafe 47 Bute Street Prince Edward

bar-leone.w: A small, warm Roman style neighbourhood bar that was named the World's Best Bar in 2025 and is No. 3 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026. Simple, perfect Italian drinks, vinyl on the turntable and a crowd spilling onto the street.
bar-leone.t: 11-15 Bridges Street, Central. From 17:00 until late. Walk-in only, no bookings, and queues of an hour or more on busy nights. Mid priced.

coa.w: A tiny agave bar with a 41 page menu of tequila and mezcal, and among the most awarded bars in Asia: No. 24 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026. Bright, clever cocktails that even non tequila drinkers love.
coa.t: Shop A, LG/F, Wah Shin House, 6-10 Shin Hing Street, Central, near Hollywood Road. Tue to Sun 18:00 to midnight, Fri and Sat to 01:00. Closed Monday. No bookings: leave your number with the door staff to join the waitlist.
coa.m: COA bar Shin Hing Street Central

argo.w: The bar at the Four Seasons, with big windows over Victoria Harbour and a menu built around ingredients under threat from climate change. No. 37 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026. Polished, calm and a great place for the view.
argo.t: 1/F, Four Seasons Hotel, Central. Mon to Thu 17:00 to 01:00, Fri and Sat to 02:00. Book online or on +852 3196 8882. Smart casual, no beachwear or sportswear.
argo.m: ARGO Four Seasons Hotel Hong Kong

darkside.w: The Rosewood's moody bar of dark spirits, cognac and cigars, with live jazz every night. Multi award winning in Time Out's bar awards, and ten minutes' walk along the waterfront from the Sheraton.
darkside.t: 2/F, Rosewood Hong Kong, Victoria Dockside. Sun to Thu 17:00 to midnight, Fri and Sat to 01:00. Jazz from 20:15 Tue to Thu. Book online or +852 3891 8732. Smart casual, sleeved shirts and covered shoes.

sky-lounge.w: The bar on the top floor of your hotel, looking straight across the harbour to the Island skyline. Cocktails, wine and afternoon tea, with a front row seat for A Symphony of Lights at 20:00.
sky-lounge.m: Sky Lounge Sheraton Hong Kong Hotel

chi-lin.n: Chi Lin Nunnery and Nan Lian Garden
chi-lin.l: 志蓮淨苑 南蓮園池
chi-lin.w: A Buddhist nunnery of dark timber halls built without a single nail, set among lotus ponds, with a classical Tang dynasty style garden across the road. A golden pavilion, bonsai and a waterfall, all with the tower blocks of Kowloon behind.
chi-lin.t: Free. Nan Lian Garden 07:00 to 21:00. The nunnery halls close earlier, in the late afternoon. Diamond Hill MTR, exit C2, about 25 minutes from TST.

hkmoa.w: The city's main art museum, right on the TST waterfront next to the Star Ferry. Chinese painting, calligraphy and ceramics alongside modern Hong Kong art, in galleries with big windows onto the harbour.
hkmoa.t: Free, except special exhibitions. Mon to Wed and Fri 10:00 to 18:00, weekends to 21:00. Closed Thursday.
hkmoa.m: Hong Kong Museum of Art Salisbury Road

ladies-market.w: A kilometre of stalls on Tung Choi Street in Mong Kok, selling clothes, bags, phone cases and souvenirs, with bargaining expected. Around it: Sneakers Street on Fa Yuen Street and the Goldfish Market, with fish hanging in bags outside the shops.
ladies-market.t: Stalls from around midday to late evening. Mong Kok MTR, three stops north of TST. Cash for the stalls.
ladies-market.m: Ladies Market Tung Choi Street Mong Kok

tai-o.w: A fishing village on the far west of Lantau where families still live in houses on stilts over the tidal creeks. Lanes of drying fish and shrimp paste, small temples, and boat trips out to look for the pink dolphins.
tai-o.t: Bus 21 from Ngong Ping, about 20 minutes, then bus 11 to Tung Chung MTR. Allow two to three hours. Cash or Octopus.

areas.name: Shibuya
areas.meta: With Harajuku, Omotesando, Daikanyama and Ebisu.

must.line: Thick pork cutlet in crisp panko, with shredded cabbage and a sweet, fruity sauce.
Rare crumbed beef cutlet you sear yourself, piece by piece, on a hot stone.
A clear salt and chicken broth lifted with yuzu citrus, Tokyo's lighter style of ramen.
Sushi handed straight from the chef, eaten in one bite within seconds of being made.
Skewers of every part of the chicken, grilled over charcoal, best with a cold beer.
Whisky and very fizzy soda over ice, the drink of every Tokyo bar and izakaya.

items.one: Famous Dutch pancake breakfast in Tomigaya
items.fits: Sun 18 slow breakfast. It is about 15 minutes' walk from the hotel and on the way to Meiji Jingū through Yoyogi Park. Go at 08:00 rather than 09:00 to beat the queue.

items.one: Norwegian coffee and mid century chairs in Tomigaya
items.fits: Mon 19 late breakfast. Open from 07:00 every day including Monday, when Path is closed, and an easy 15 minute walk from the hotel.

items.one: Classic tonkatsu in an old Omotesando bathhouse
items.fits: Sat 17 lunch in Omotesando. It is two minutes off the avenue, open all afternoon, and a filling first proper meal after the flight.

items.one: Light, citrusy yuzu ramen near Harajuku
items.fits: Sun 18 lunch in Harajuku. A quick, light bowl between Meiji Jingū and the festival streets. It is a few minutes north of Takeshita Street.

items.one: Rare beef cutlet you finish on a hot stone
items.fits: Mon 19 lunch in Omotesando at 14:00. After the lunch rush the queue is shortest, and it is a short walk from the vintage stores.

items.one: Standing sushi counter, piece by piece
items.fits: Sat 17 dinner close to the hotel if you would rather not book: quick, cheap and ten minutes' walk. Also a good snack stop any evening.

items.one: Cheap, fast touch-screen sushi.
items.fits: A quick lunch or a late bite. Five minutes from the Hachikō exit.

items.one: Proper wagyu burger, five minutes from the hotel
items.fits: Sat 17 dinner if jet lag wins: five minutes' walk, open late, no booking. Or any late night after a big day.

items.one: Regional food counters under the hotel.
items.fits: An easy dinner any night back at the hotel, or after a late arrival.

items.one: Fun surf-shack seafood izakaya in Shibuya
items.fits: Sat 17 dinner close by: a cheerful first night about 12 minutes' walk from the hotel. Book an 18:30 table.

items.one: Omakase sushi counter, about 20 courses
items.fits: Sun 18 nice dinner. Ten minutes' walk from the hotel, on the quieter side of the station away from the festival crowds. Book a 19:00 or 19:30 seat to allow for getting back from the karts.

items.one: Tiny izakaya under one roof.
items.fits: Dinner on a free evening. Sun 18 after Street Kart, or Tue 20 if back early.

items.one: Award winning cocktails, 8 minutes from Shibuya
items.fits: A nightcap after Sun 18 nice dinner, or any evening. It is a short walk from the hotel.

items.one: Rooftop cocktails above the Scramble
items.fits: Sat 17 after dinner if you have energy left, for a second look at the lights after Shibuya Sky. Or a drink before Sun 18 nice dinner.

items.one: Eight seat absinthe speakeasy in Ebisu
items.fits: Pairs with an Ebisu Yokochō night, five minutes' walk apart. Not on a set slot, but a strong option for Sun 18 after dinner.

items.one: Tiny vinyl listening bar, 10,000 records
items.fits: Sat 17 after dinner near Dōgenzaka. Low key and quiet, ideal for a first jet lagged night.

items.one: The Scramble Crossing from above, drink in hand.
items.fits: Best at dusk or after dark. Fits any Shibuya evening, three minutes from the crossing.

items.one: Free window view of the crossing and the trains.
items.fits: Any time to midnight. Pairs with a walk past the station.

items.one: Nintendo Tokyo and the Pokémon Center on 6F.
items.fits: While Cynthia shops Omotesando. Also in How-to 4.

items.one: New design building, rooftop and Kosugi-yu bathhouse.
items.fits: Opposite Tokyu Plaza. Fits Sat 17 or Mon 19 around Omotesando.

items.one: Mirror escalator and a free rooftop terrace.
items.fits: At the Harajuku crossing. Five minutes from Takeshita Street on Sun 18.

items.one: Back-street labels, sneakers and vintage.
items.fits: Either side of Cat Street, so it slots into Sat 17 morning.

items.one: Nine floors of music, freshly renovated.
items.fits: Five minutes from the hotel. Good for a wet hour.

items.one: Design shops and the T-Site bookshop.
items.fits: A swap for Sun 18 morning instead of Meiji Jingū. Pairs with Nakameguro.

items.one: Canal-side boutiques and the Roastery.
items.fits: With Daikanyama, or a slow coffee morning on its own.

items.one: Lawns, ginkgo and the Sunday rockabilly dancers.
items.fits: Next door to Meiji Jingū. Add it to Sun 18 after the shrine.

items.one: Head spa, English spoken.
items.fits: Five minutes from the hotel. Book ahead.

items.one: Head spa in the Omotesando back streets.
items.fits: Open to 22:00, so it works after dinner. Book ahead.

items.one: Body and foot massage, east side of the station.
Body and foot massage in Dōgenzaka.
items.fits: Open 24 hours. Walk-ins usually fine.

areas.name: Shinjuku
areas.meta: East and west Shinjuku, Kabukichō, Golden Gai, Shinjuku-sanchōme, Nishi-Shinjuku and Shin-Ōkubo.

must.line: Thick cold noodles dipped into a rich, concentrated hot broth.
Prawns, fish and vegetables in a whisper of batter, straight from the oil.
Ramen built on dried sardines: bold, briny and very Tokyo.
Japan's prized fruit layered in a tall glass with cream and ice cream.
A seasonal procession of small, exquisite courses.
Wagashi and pastries boxed like jewellery in the department store basement.

items.one: Tokyo's favourite tsukemen, near the south exit
items.fits: Mon 19 at 17:00 when it reopens, as a filling start before Omoide Yokochō. Open Mondays, closed Sundays.

items.one: Tempura counter in sesame oil since the 1920s
items.fits: Mon 19 dinner instead of grazing at Omoide. On the east side near Shinjuku-sanchōme, so it suits the walk from Kabukichō towards Golden Gai.

items.one: Intense sardine ramen up a Golden Gai stair
items.fits: Mon 19 at 21:00, a late bowl in Golden Gai before the Fukutoshin line home. Open all night.

items.one: Fruit parfaits under Shinjuku's luxury fruit shop
items.fits: Mon 19 at 16:45 after the 3D cat, three minutes away. Or dessert after dinner, last orders 20:30.

items.one: Tokyo's grandest depachika food hall
items.fits: Mon 19 at 16:45, beside Shinjuku-sanchōme, for sweets and a snack before the evening. Also a rainy day stop.

items.one: Kyoto kaiseki courses by the east exit
items.fits: Mon 19 special dinner at 18:00 in place of Omoide, then Kabukichō and Golden Gai after. Last orders 20:00.

items.one: World famous farm-to-glass cocktail counter
items.fits: Mon 19 nightcap after Golden Gai, 15 minutes' walk west. Open to 02:00 and Monday is a quiet night. Taxi home after the trains.

items.one: 52nd floor jazz bar from Lost in Translation
items.fits: Mon 19 at 17:00 for sunset (about 17:00) instead of the 3D cat, then down to Omoide. Arrive before 20:00 to skip the music charge.

items.one: Free deck 202 metres up in west Shinjuku
items.fits: Mon 19 at 16:15 for dusk, leaving the hotel at 15:45. Both decks are open that day. Then ten minutes' walk to Omoide Yokochō for 17:30.

items.one: Formal gardens and lawns by Shinjuku
items.fits: Closed Mondays, so not on Mon 19. Works as a swap for Sun 18 morning instead of Meiji Jingū. Closes 16:00 in October.

items.one: Five floors of Japanese craft and labels
items.fits: Mon 19 at 16:45 if you come early, five minutes from the 3D cat. Closes 20:00.

items.one: Free projection show on the Tocho towers
items.fits: Mon 19 at 18:00, pairs with the deck: leave Omoide at 17:45, watch, then head east to Kabukichō by 18:45.

items.one: Big hot spring bath in Kabukichō
items.fits: Mon 19 late, a soak after Golden Gai. Open all night, but the late surcharge applies, so earlier is cheaper.

items.one: Koreatown: K-pop, skincare, street food
items.fits: One stop on the Yamanote. Mon 19 at 15:30 instead of resting at the hotel, then walk down to Shinjuku for 16:45.

areas.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen is closed on Mondays, so it only fits a swap day, and its gates close at 16:00 in October. Both Tocho decks are open on Mon 19. Fūunji and BenFiddich close on Sundays, fine for Monday. Takano Fruit Parlour hours are from 2022, so check on the day. Nothing here needs booking this week: book Kakiden or a New York Bar window seat only if you want them.

areas.name: Yokohama and Kamakura
areas.meta: Minato Mirai, Chinatown, Yamashita Park, Motomachi and the Yamate Bluff, with Kamakura further out.

must.line: A giant steamed pork bun, the Chinatown street snack.
Ketchup spaghetti with ham and peppers, a Yokohama hotel invention.
Crème caramel dressed with fruit and cream, born at the same hotel.
Silky tofu in a numbing, chilli bean sauce.
Crisp lacquered skin rolled in thin pancakes, the banquet centrepiece.
Tiny local whitebait piled on rice, Kamakura's signature dish.

items.one: Napolitan and pudding à la mode, where both began
items.fits: Tue 20 lunch at 13:00, facing Yamashita Park, so the afternoon walk into Chinatown starts at the door.

items.one: Waterfront pier of open kitchen restaurants
items.fits: Tue 20 lunch at 13:00 if you would rather stay in Minato Mirai, 12 minutes from the Red Brick Warehouses.

items.one: Chinatown's giant pork buns, eaten on the street
items.fits: Tue 20 afternoon as you reach Chinatown, a snack before dinner. Closes 19:30 on weekdays.

items.one: Sichuan mapo tofu and hot pot
items.fits: Tue 20 Chinatown dinner at 17:30, the relaxed choice. Weekday last orders 20:00.

items.one: Japan's oldest Chinese restaurant, Cantonese
items.fits: Tue 20 Chinatown dinner at 17:30, on the main street. Good for Peking duck and dim sum.

items.one: Grand Cantonese banquet, Chinatown since the 1890s
items.fits: Tue 20 special dinner at 17:30. The ¥11,000 course is the sweet spot. Book a table this month.

items.one: Classic British bar in the 1927 New Grand
items.fits: Tue 20 at 17:00, a pre-dinner cocktail five minutes from Chinatown.

items.one: 70th floor lounge over the harbour
items.fits: Only if you flip Tue 20: Chinatown for lunch, then Minato Mirai at dusk with a drink here from 17:30.

items.one: Free wave-shaped deck facing the skyline
items.fits: Tue 20 afternoon, on the harbour walk between Red Brick and Yamashita Park. Back after dinner for the night view.

items.one: 69th floor deck over the port
items.fits: Tue 20 at 11:30, beside Sakuragichō as you arrive, before the Air Cabin. Fuji on a clear morning.

items.one: Lattice tower deck at the end of Yamashita Park
items.fits: Tue 20 at 19:00 after dinner, a minute from the station, then the 19:30 train. Night tickets from 18:00.

items.one: Old foreign hilltop: houses, cemetery, harbour view
items.fits: Tue 20 at 15:30, up from Yamashita Park, then down through Motomachi into Chinatown. Houses close 17:00.

items.one: Old fashioned boutique street below the Bluff
items.fits: Tue 20 at 16:30, on the way down from Yamate to Chinatown dinner.

items.one: Samurai capital: temples, shrine, Great Buddha
items.fits: Dropped from Tue 20, but it could replace Minato Mirai: Tsukiji, then Kamakura from about 11:30, then the JR Yokosuka line to Yokohama for Chinatown dinner.

items.one: The 13th century bronze Buddha, in the open
items.fits: Part of a Kamakura swap on Tue 20. Open 08:00 to 17:00 in October, ¥300, plus ¥50 to go inside.

items.one: Hillside temple with a sea view terrace
items.fits: Five minutes from the Great Buddha, so pair them. 08:00 to 17:00, last entry 16:30, ¥400.

items.one: Little seaside train between the sights
items.fits: Kamakura Station to Hase, three stops, for the Buddha and Hase-dera. Suica works.

items.one: Kamakura's great shrine up the stone steps
items.fits: Ten minutes' walk from Kamakura Station. Grounds 06:00 to 20:00, free.

items.one: Snack and sweet lane to the shrine
items.fits: Between Kamakura Station and Hachimangū, so it is lunch on the way: shirasu and street snacks.

areas.notes: The Cup Noodles Museum in Minato Mirai is closed on Tuesdays, so it is left out. Weekday Chinatown kitchens close early: Jukeihanten last orders 20:00, Edosei shuts 19:30, which suits the 19:30 train. Manchinrō and Heichinrō have irregular closed days, so check the Tuesday when booking. In Kamakura the Buddha and Hase-dera close at 17:00, so a Kamakura swap needs to reach Kamakura by about 11:30.

areas.name: Kyoto
areas.meta: With Pontochō and Kiyamachi, Gion and Higashiyama, Arashiyama, Kyoto Station and Fushimi.

must.line: Kyoto's formal seasonal dinner of many small courses, the city's great food tradition.
Silky tofu simmered at the table in kelp broth, made with Kyoto's soft water.
Kyoto home cooking: small plates of simmered vegetables, yuba and fish.
Uji matcha with warabi mochi or kuzukiri in black sugar syrup.
Clear soy and pork broth, thin noodles and a pile of Kujō green onion.
Kyoto's signature sweet: soft cinnamon rice dough folded around red bean paste.
Soft, smooth sake from the city's own brewing district, best as a tasting flight.

items.one: Latte on the river by Togetsukyō bridge
items.fits: Fri 23 coffee at 10:15. A few minutes' walk from the bridge and the river path. Take it to the bank, as there is almost no seating.

items.one: Toast-your-own warabi mochi and matcha
items.fits: Fri 23 at 10:15 if you want to sit down rather than queue for coffee. Near Tenryū-ji and the station.

items.one: Tofu hotpot set in a garden house
items.fits: Fri 23 early lunch at 11:00 in Arashiyama instead of Nishiki, if the morning runs long. Skip the market and go straight to the rest at the hotel.

items.one: Kyoto small plates on the Pontochō alley
items.fits: Wed 21 casual dinner at 19:00. Right on Pontochō, two minutes from Shijō Bridge. Graze on obanzai and yakitori.

items.one: Kyoto's most famous gyoza, on Kiyamachi
items.fits: Wed 21 dinner if Pontochō looks full or pricey. Open from 17:00 to 02:00 on a Wednesday, so it also works as a late bite.

items.one: Obanzai counter since 1939, Bib Gourmand
items.fits: Closed Wednesday, so it only works if you swap the dinners and eat in Gion on Wednesday. Then it is Fri 23 at 17:30 on Kiyamachi.

items.one: Classic Kyoto shoyu ramen by the station
items.fits: Sat 24 at 10:45 after check-out, instead of an ekiben. Five minutes from Kyoto Station, quick turnover. Be out by 11:30 for the 12:01.

items.one: Kuzukiri and matcha in a Gion tea room
items.fits: Fri 23 at about 17:30 on the way down into Gion, if you skip the pagoda drink. On Shijō-dōri, two minutes from Yasaka Shrine.

items.one: Course tempura in a Gion teahouse
items.fits: Fri 23 special dinner at 18:30. Five minutes' walk from Yasaka Pagoda, so it follows the sunset perfectly. The ¥16,000 Rokuhara course keeps it inside budget.

items.one: Seasonal kaiseki by the Shirakawa canal
items.fits: Fri 23 special dinner at 18:30. The classic Kyoto kaiseki at the gentle end of the budget, in the prettiest lanes of Gion.

items.one: Quiet Kyoto dinner course in north Gion
items.fits: Fri 23 special dinner at 18:30, if Endo and Nakatani are full. Near the top of your budget.

items.one: Rooftop drink level with Yasaka Pagoda
items.fits: Fri 23 at 17:15, straight after the pagoda at sunset. Then five minutes downhill to an 18:30 dinner at Endo.

items.one: Asia's 50 Best speakeasy behind a bookshelf
items.fits: Wed 21 after Pontochō dinner, about ten minutes' walk north. Or Fri 23 after Gion. Closed Sundays.

items.one: Magician-themed cocktails with swing seats
items.fits: Wed 21 nightcap from 20:00, a few minutes from Pontochō and Kiyamachi.

items.one: Tiny sake bar with tasting flights in English
items.fits: Wed 21 after dinner, a short taxi north of Pontochō. Check it is open that night first.

items.one: Up the white tower opposite the station
items.fits: Wed 21 at 17:25 instead of the station building, for the city at dusk. Or Sat 24 if Inari finishes early.

items.one: 1,001 golden Kannon statues in one hall
items.fits: Fri 23 at 14:30, cutting the rest short. Then a five minute taxi up to Kiyomizu-dera for 15:30. Closes 17:00.

items.one: Zen gardens and a bamboo grove off Ninenzaka
items.fits: Fri 23 at about 16:45, between Ninenzaka and the pagoda. Last entry is about 17:00, so go straight there off the steps.

items.one: Twin dragon ceiling behind the Gion teahouses
items.fits: Fri 23 if you swap Kiyomizu for a slower Gion afternoon. Two minutes from Endo, closes 17:00.

items.one: Giant wooden hall on the walk to the station
items.fits: Sat 24 at 10:30 on the walk from the hotel to Kyoto Station, right on Karasuma-dōri. Or Fri 23 in the rest window.

items.one: The Silver Pavilion and its sand garden
items.fits: The northern Higashiyama half day. Fri 23 at 13:15 instead of resting, then the path south and a taxi to Kiyomizu at 15:30. Closes 17:00.

items.one: Canal-side path linking the eastern temples
items.fits: Walk it south from Ginkaku-ji, past Hōnen-in, to Nanzen-ji. About 30 minutes without stops.

items.one: Thatched gate and sand mounds, rarely busy
items.fits: Five minutes off the Philosopher's Path. Grounds are free and close at 16:00.

items.one: Huge gate and a red brick aqueduct
items.fits: The south end of the Philosopher's Path. Taxi from here to Kiyomizu-dera is about ten minutes.

items.one: Matcha town and the Phoenix Hall
items.fits: A swap for the Fri 23 Arashiyama morning if the bamboo grove fails you, or if Thursday and Friday get reshuffled. 20 minutes on the JR Nara line.

items.one: Sake warehouses and a tasting, south of Inari
items.fits: Sat 24 only if you come down the mountain by 09:00 and ask for an 11:00 check-out. Two stops on the Keihan line from Inari.

items.one: Body and foot massage, closest to the hotel
items.fits: Fri 23 in the 12:45 rest window, a few minutes from Nishiki. Opens 12:00.

items.one: Body massage beside Nishiki Market
