items.fits: Fri 23 straight after Nishiki lunch, or Wed 21 late, open to 22:00.

items.one: Head spa near Shijō-Karasuma
items.fits: Fri 23 in the rest window. One subway stop from the hotel. Book ahead.

items.one: Head spa at Shijō-Kawaramachi
items.fits: Fri 23 after Nishiki, at the east end of the arcades. Closes 19:00. Book ahead.

areas.notes: Book the Fri 23 Gion dinner this week: Endo Yasaka on TableCheck is the strongest pick, Nakatani is the cheaper kaiseki (closed Sundays only). Menami is closed Wednesdays, so it only fits if you swap the two dinners. Daiichi Asahi is closed Thursdays, no clash. Bee's Knees is closed Sundays, Kagizen Mondays, no clash. Jidai Matsuri, Kyoto's big costume parade, is on Thu 22 from about 12:00 (Imperial Palace to Heian Shrine), and the Kurama Fire Festival is that night: no clash while you are in Osaka, but if you swap Thursday and Friday, expect crowds and road closures in the centre. Hours for eX café, Yudofu Sagano, Sake Bar Yoramu, K36 and the temples were not all confirmed for 2026: check Google Maps the day before.

areas.name: Nara
areas.meta: Nara Park, Sanjō-dōri and the old Naramachi quarter.

must.line: Cured mackerel or salmon on pressed rice, wrapped in a persimmon leaf.
Mugwort rice cake pounded at speed in front of you, filled with red bean.
Udon hidden inside a fried tofu pouch tied up like a purse.
Vegetables pickled for months in sake lees, dark, sweet and boozy.
Nara calls itself the birthplace of refined sake. Taste five at the brewery.

items.one: Udon tucked inside a fried tofu purse
items.fits: Wed 21 lunch at 12:00 if you would rather sit down than grab kakinoha. Ten minutes south of Sanjō-dōri, so it costs you about 15 minutes overall.

items.one: Thatched teahouse in the woods
items.fits: Wed 21 at about 14:15, right on your walk from Kasuga Taisha to Tōdai-ji. Matcha and a sweet under the trees.

items.one: Five sake tasting at a Naramachi brewery
items.fits: Wed 21 only if you do Naramachi instead of Nigatsu-dō. Daytime only.

items.one: Ashura and Kōfuku-ji's great statues
items.fits: Wed 21 at 12:45 as you pass Kōfuku-ji, if lunch is quick. The pagoda is wrapped, but the museum is open.

items.one: Stroll garden that borrows Tōdai-ji's roof
items.fits: Wed 21 at 15:30 instead of Nigatsu-dō, five minutes west of the Nandaimon gate. Closed Tuesdays, so Wednesday is fine. Last entry about 16:00.

items.one: Moss and pond gardens, free with a passport
items.fits: Next door to Isuien, so add it on Wed 21 at about 16:00. Bring passports.

items.one: Old merchant lanes south of the park
items.fits: Wed 21 as a swap for the Tōdai-ji hill if the day runs late: ten minutes south of Kōfuku-ji, and a short walk to JR Nara for the train.

items.one: Walk through a restored townhouse
items.fits: In Naramachi, with Harushika and Mentoan. Closed Mondays, open Wednesday.

items.one: Nara linen and tea towels since 1716
items.fits: In Naramachi. Good small gifts if you do the old town.

items.one: The world's oldest wooden buildings
items.fits: Not on this trip's Nara afternoon. It is a separate half day, about 15 minutes by JR from Nara plus a 20 minute walk, and only works if you drop Osaka or Arashiyama.

areas.notes: Isuien is closed Tuesdays, so Wed 21 is fine. Kōfuku-ji is only passed in the plan, so the National Treasure Museum is listed as the add-on, not the temple itself. Naramachi shops and the Kōshi-no-ie close around 17:00. Hours for Mentoan, Mizuya Chaya, Harushika and Yoshikien were not confirmed for 2026: check Google Maps the night before.

areas.name: Osaka
areas.meta: Day trip from Kyoto: Osaka Castle, Umeda, Kuromon, Horie, Namba, Shinsekai, Dōtonbori and Hōzenji Yokochō.

must.line: Octopus in a molten dashi batter ball, crisp outside, far too hot to eat straight away.
A cabbage and batter pancake cooked on the griddle in front of you, with sweet sauce and mayonnaise.
Okonomiyaki's lighter cousin, packed with spring onion and finished with soy and lemon.
Crumbed, deep fried skewers dipped once in a shared pot of thin sauce. Never twice.
Osaka's own udon, in a clear dashi with sweet simmered fried tofu on top.
A big, soft steamed pork bun, the snack every Osakan brings home.

items.one: Rice flour bakery inside the castle park
items.fits: Thu 22 takeaway breakfast at 08:30. Open from 07:00, so buy curry bread and coffee and eat on a bench below the walls.

items.one: Osaka's famous steamed pork bun
items.fits: Thu 22: grab a hot butaman on the walk from Kuromon or before Dōtonbori at 18:30. Or buy a box at Osaka Station for the train home.

items.one: Kuromon's tuna specialist, eat at the counter
items.fits: Thu 22 Kuromon lunch at 12:00. Make this the first stop: a fatty tuna and seared belly plate, then graze on from there.

items.one: Uni, oysters and sushi with somewhere to sit
items.fits: Thu 22 Kuromon lunch, second stop. The eat-in area is a welcome seat after the morning on your feet.

items.one: Where kitsune udon was invented, 1893
items.fits: Thu 22 during the Shinsaibashi run around 14:00, as a light second lunch. Open Thursday, closed Sundays.

items.one: The original kushikatsu, under Tsūtenkaku
items.fits: Thu 22 Shinsekai snack at dusk, about 17:00. Open all day, so a quick plate of five skewers and a beer, then on to Dōtonbori.

items.one: Locals' kushikatsu counter in Janjan-Yokochō
items.fits: Thu 22 Shinsekai snack on the way in at 16:15. Open Thursday. Yaekatsu next door is closed on Thursdays.

items.one: The best takoyaki in Namba, crisp and molten
items.fits: Thu 22 Dōtonbori eat standing up from 18:30. Five minutes south of the canal. Kukuru on Ebisu bridge, under the giant octopus, is the photo-friendly backup.

items.one: Negiyaki and okonomiyaki, loud and local
items.fits: Thu 22 dinner from 18:30. Opens 17:00 on weekdays, five minutes from Dōtonbori. Put your name down first, then wander for takoyaki while you wait.

items.one: Dōtonbori's classic okonomiyaki since 1945
items.fits: Thu 22 dinner at 18:30 if open: one listing says it closes on Thursdays, so check Google Maps that morning. Fukutarō is the safe swap.

items.one: Kitsune udon in a calm old udon house
items.fits: Thu 22 on Dōtonbori around 18:30 if you want to sit down for ten minutes of quiet. Last orders 20:00.

items.one: Wobbly cheesecake, warm from the oven
items.fits: Thu 22 between Namba Yasaka and Shinsekai, or after Dōtonbori. Five minutes from Namba Station, open to 20:00.

items.one: Red bean soup for two beside the mossy statue
items.fits: Thu 22 Hōzenji Yokochō at 20:30, as dessert before the quiet drink. Open to 22:00.

items.one: Crab feast under the giant moving crab
items.fits: Thu 22 dinner at 18:30 if you would rather sit down than graze. Right on Dōtonbori. Book a table online this week.

items.one: Robata grill and sake in Hōzenji Yokochō
items.fits: Thu 22 quiet drink at 20:30, a few steps from Mizukake Fudō. Sake and a skewer or two before the train.

items.one: 36th floor cocktails over the Namba neon
items.fits: Thu 22 after Hōzenji, on top of Namba Station, so it is on the way to the Midōsuji line home. Open to 23:30 on Thursdays.

items.one: Asia's 50 Best cocktail bar, ten seats
items.fits: Thu 22 nightcap on the way home: five minutes from Osaka Station, before the JR special rapid to Kyoto. Open Thursday, closed Sundays.

items.one: No menu, drinks made to your taste
items.fits: Thu 22 after Hōzenji if you are happy to catch a later train. Ten minutes' walk to Amerikamura, open to 03:00.

items.one: Osaka's highest deck, 300 metres up
items.fits: The weather fallback for Thu 22: if Umeda Sky was clouded out, go at sunset, ten minutes' walk from Shinsekai. 09:00 to 22:00, about ¥2,000.

items.one: Flea market day: Thu 22 is market day
items.fits: Thu 22 swap for part of the Horie shopping: the monthly market runs on the 22nd, and the temple is 15 minutes' walk from Shinsekai. Go before 16:00.

items.one: Knives, takoyaki pans and plastic food
items.fits: Thu 22 straight after Kuromon lunch: it runs between the market and Namba, so it costs almost no extra walking.

items.one: Pokémon Center and Nintendo store, one floor
items.fits: Thu 22 near Umeda Sky in the morning, or on the way home, above Osaka Station. Open to 20:00.

items.one: Back-street izakaya and standing bars
items.fits: Thu 22 instead of Hōzenji if you want more noise, not less. Five minutes east of Namba Station.

items.one: Old wooden-house cafés and a river island
items.fits: Dropped from Thu 22. If the castle runs short, Nakazakichō is ten minutes' walk from Umeda Sky.

items.one: Ancient shrine and the red arched bridge
items.fits: A swap for the Horie shopping on Thu 22. Ten minutes by Nankai local train from Namba. Closes 17:00.

items.one: Super Nintendo World and the big theme park
items.fits: You chose against it, to spend the day in the city. Kept only in case Thu 22 changes completely.

areas.notes: Thursday closures on Thu 22: Yaekatsu, the best known kushikatsu counter in Janjan-Yokochō, is closed on Thursdays, so use Tengu in the same alley or Daruma under the tower. Okonomiyaki Mizuno may also be closed on Thursdays (sources disagree), so check Google Maps that morning and fall back to Fukutarō. Okazu Izakaya Kuu, a small sake izakaya by Hōzenji, is also closed Thursdays. Thu 22 is Shitennō-ji flea market day (21st and 22nd each month). Nothing needs booking this week; Kani Dōraku is the only place worth booking, and only if you want a sit-down dinner. The HEP Five Ferris wheel in Umeda was closed for works from October 2025, so it is left out. Kuromon stalls wind down from about 16:00 and like cash.

areas.name: Ginza and east Tokyo
areas.meta: With Hibiya, Yūrakuchō, Marunouchi, Shimbashi, Tsukiji, Toranomon, Azabudai, Asakusa, Kuramae and Odaiba.

must.line: Tokyo's gooey, griddle-fried batter of cabbage and seafood, scraped off the hotplate with tiny spatulas.
Each piece fried to order and handed straight across, crisp, light and never greasy.
A thick pork cutlet in soft white bread with tonkatsu sauce, the classic Tokyo takeaway.
Ginza's own invention: a soft bun of sweet red bean paste, topped with a salted cherry blossom.
A crumbed, deep-fried mince patty, eaten hot in the street in Asakusa.
Skewers off the charcoal and a cold beer while the trains rumble overhead.

items.one: 18-dish temple breakfast in Tsukiji
items.fits: Sun 25 slow breakfast. Taxi 5 minutes from the hotel, be there by 08:00 at the weekend, then taxi on to the East Gardens. Sotoroku on the hotel's 18F (buffet to 10:00) is the no-effort fallback.

items.one: Good coffee by Kamiyachō Station
items.fits: Mon 26 after teamLab at about 10:40, if you skip Sky Room or want a coffee for the train. In the basement of Garden Plaza, on your way to Kamiyachō.

items.one: The bakery that invented anpan, 1874
items.fits: Sun 25 afternoon in Ginza. It is on the 4-chōme crossing beside the Wakō clock tower. Grab a cherry blossom anpan as you pass.

items.one: Ginza's oldest tonkatsu and a famous katsu sando
items.fits: Sun 25 'eat in the complexes' evening, ten minutes from the hotel. Or Mon 26 after Shimbashi: take away a katsu sando for the 06:22 start to Haneda.

items.one: Walk-in tempura on Matsuya's 8F
items.fits: Sun 25 'eat in the complexes' evening. Matsuya's 8F restaurant floor trades to 22:00, well after the shops close, with an English menu.

items.one: Japan's oldest beer hall, built 1934
items.fits: Sun 25 dinner if you want something louder than a restaurant floor. On Chūō-dōri in 7-chōme, eight minutes' walk back to the hotel.

items.one: Monjayaki on Tsukishima's Monja Street
items.fits: Sun 25 dinner as a change from Ginza. Yūrakuchō line from Ginza-itchōme, two stops, or a 10 minute taxi. Open from 11:30 on Sundays.

items.one: Counter tempura course on Ginza Six 13F
items.fits: Sun 25 nice dinner, no extra travel: book an 18:00 counter seat on TableCheck, after the Ginza Six rooftop. Top of your budget, so check the course price when booking.

items.one: All-you-can-eat sushi on a double-decker tour
items.fits: Sun 25 evening: the 17:00 or 19:00 departure from Kajibashi car park near Tokyo Station, 15 minutes from Ginza. ¥16,000 each, sushi and drinks included.

items.one: Classic Asakusa tendon since 1887
items.fits: Mon 26 lunch at about 13:30 after Kappabashi. The queue is shorter after the noon rush. Cash only.

items.one: Hot menchi katsu to eat in the street
items.fits: Mon 26, a snack between Kappabashi and Sensō-ji, or instead of a sit-down lunch. Two minutes from Kaminarimon.

items.one: Big sashimi platters, Shimbashi seafood izakaya
items.fits: Mon 26 Shimbashi dinner at 19:00. A minute from the station, packed on a Monday night. Order the six-kind sashimi platter.

items.one: Smoky skewers under the Yūrakuchō tracks
items.fits: Mon 26 dinner, ten minutes' walk from Shimbashi along the tracks. Or graze here first, then finish in Shimbashi.

items.one: Classic Ginza cocktails, the sidecar is the order
items.fits: Sun 25 after dinner. It is closed on Monday, so Sunday is your night for it. Go before 21:00 for a counter seat.

items.one: World-famous bar, no menu, made to your taste
items.fits: Mon 26 after the Shimbashi dinner, ten minutes' walk into Ginza. Closed Sundays, so Monday is your night. Arrive soon after 20:00.

items.one: 24th floor cocktails over Hibiya Park
items.fits: Sun 25 at dusk (sunset about 16:55) instead of the department store rooftops. Opens 15:00 on Sundays, ten minutes from the hotel.

items.one: Free 46th floor view over the bay
items.fits: Any evening on the walk home, five minutes from the hotel. Mon 26 late, a last look at Tokyo lit up before the early flight.

items.one: Bayside garden with a teahouse on the pond
items.fits: Sun 25 instead of the East Gardens, ten minutes' walk from the hotel. Or Tue 20 straight after the Tsukiji breakfast if you finish early: it opens at 09:00, five minutes away.

items.one: Bean to bar chocolate in quiet Kuramae
items.fits: Mon 26 between Kappabashi and Sensō-ji, or a dry stop on a wet day. 15 minutes' walk south of Kappabashi.

items.one: Izakaya and yakitori in the railway arches
items.fits: Mon 26 19:00 alternative to Shimbashi, ten minutes' walk. Andy's Shin-Hinomoto by exit C1 is the English-friendly start. Mostly cash.

items.one: Bayside malls, beach and promenade
items.fits: Sat 24, if check-in is quick, go out at 15:00 rather than 16:00 and walk the Odaiba Seaside Park boardwalk before the fireworks. Note the Unicorn Gundam statue ended its display in August 2026.

items.one: Late head spa in Ginza 2-chōme
items.fits: Sun 25 after the shops close, before a late dinner. Open to 23:00.

items.one: Head spa in Ginza 1-chōme
items.fits: Sun 25 mid afternoon, a break from the department stores. Open 10:00 to 22:00.

items.one: Thai massage five minutes from the hotel
items.fits: Sat 24 after the fireworks (open to midnight), or Mon 26 after dinner while you pack in your head.

items.one: Late bodywork in Ginza 7-chōme
items.fits: Mon 26 late after Shimbashi, open to midnight. Legs will need it after Asakusa.

areas.notes: Kabuki-za's October run ends on 20 October, so there is no kabuki on your Ginza days. Star Bar is closed on Mondays and Bar High Five on Sundays: one each night. Book Tempura Yamanoue (TableCheck) or the Sushi Bus (sushi-bus.com) this week if you want either for Sun 25. Tonton and Monja Kondo hours come from older listings, so check Google Maps on the day. The Unicorn Gundam at DiverCity Odaiba came down at the end of August 2026.

areas.name: Japan other
areas.meta: Experiences, shopping and day trips that are not tied to one area.

must.line: A pillowy konbini egg salad sandwich, crusts off, better than it has any right to be.
Famichiki or Karaage-kun from the hot case by the till, the perfect late night snack.
Stone-ground green tea, whisked frothy and bitter-sweet, or in parfaits and ice cream.
Delicate seasonal sweets of bean paste and rice, made to be eaten with matcha.
Try a flight of small pours, dry to fruity, then buy the bottle you liked best.
Buy a bottle to take home: Japanese labels cost less here, if you can find them.

items.one: Egg sando, onigiri and fried chicken
items.fits: Any morning, or Tue 27 breakfast before the 06:22 walk to Shimbashi. There is a konbini on every block.

items.one: Department store food halls, Ginza best
items.fits: Sun 25 while you shop Mitsukoshi and Matsuya, for a tasting lap or a picnic dinner in the room. Mon 26 for gifts to take home.

items.one: Uji matcha parfaits on Ginza Six 4F
items.fits: Sun 25 afternoon break in Ginza Six, before the rooftop garden. Go before 15:00 or after 18:00 to dodge the queue.

items.one: Imperial wagashi and matcha in Ginza 7-chōme
items.fits: Sun 25 afternoon, open on your dates. A calmer, more traditional alternative to the matcha parfait.

items.one: Sake tasting bar inside Tokyo Station
items.fits: Sat 24 as you come off the Shinkansen at 14:15, before leaving the gates, if you have energy for a quick glass. Or Sun 25 at Tokyo Station with a platform ticket.

items.one: Sumo show with dinner in Ginza
items.fits: Sun 25 at 17:00: Hirakuza Ginza, 1-9-13 Ginza, a daily 17:00 show with a kaiseki dinner, from ¥17,000 each on Klook. Or Mon 26 at 11:00 at Tokyo Sumo Club in Tokyo Tower, straight after teamLab.

items.one: Old Ginza public bath, five minutes away
items.fits: Mon 26 at about 18:00, after Asakusa and before the Shimbashi dinner. Closed Sundays.

items.one: Capsule toys, thousands of machines
items.fits: Any Shibuya evening at #C-pla, or Sun 25 at #C-pla premium in Ginza. Bring ¥100 coins.

items.one: Twelve-floor Uniqlo flagship
items.fits: Sun 25 in Ginza while Chūō-dōri is car-free. Passports for tax-free.

items.one: Flagship 100 yen shop, souvenirs and snacks
items.fits: Sun 25 in Ginza, same building as Loft. Good for cheap gifts and an extra bag.

items.one: Stationery, beauty and clever gadgets
items.fits: Sun 25 in Ginza, same building as Daiso. Loft's beauty floor has a tester bar.

items.one: Electronics, cameras and Japanese whisky
items.fits: Sun 25 on the walk from Tokyo International Forum into Ginza, or Mon 26 evening for whisky to fly home. Tax-free.

items.one: How to skip the 10% tax
items.fits: Any shopping day. Carry your passport, not a copy, and keep sealed bags sealed until you are out of Japan.

items.one: Real onsen baths at Tokyo Dome City
items.fits: A wet evening, Sun 25 or Mon 26: Marunouchi line direct from Ginza to Kōrakuen, about 12 minutes. Cheaper after 19:00.

items.one: Lost in Translation karaoke rooms, Shibuya
items.fits: A late night in Shibuya, Sat 17 or Mon 19 after Shinjuku. Close to the hotel in Udagawachō.

items.one: Photo sticker booths, open all night
items.fits: Any Shibuya evening, a minute off Center-gai and close to the hotel. Do it together: couples are fine.

items.one: Onsen, Lake Ashi and Fuji views
items.fits: Not in the plan. A whole day from Shibuya via Shinjuku, so only if you drop Kamakura and Yokohama.

items.one: Gilded shrines and October colour
items.fits: Not in the plan. Tōbu trains leave from Asakusa, so it would replace the Mon 26 Asakusa day.

areas.notes: No sumo tournament runs on your dates, so a show is the way to see it. Hirakuza Ginza refunds only 50% within 21 days and nothing within 7 days, so decide this week. Spa LaQua refuses entry with tattoos. Japan's tax-free system changes on 1 November 2026: everything you buy in October uses the current tax-off-at-the-till system. Kakigōri is a summer dish and mostly off menus by late October, so it is left out.

areas.name: Hong Kong
areas.meta: Tsim Sha Tsui, Jordan and Yau Ma Tei on the Kowloon side, with Central, SoHo and Sheung Wan across the harbour.

must.line: Steamed and fried small bites with tea: har gow, siu mai, char siu bao, ordered off a trolley or a tick sheet.
Crisp, lacquered skin over rich meat, best over rice noodles in broth. The char siu is the other must.
Thin springy egg noodles and prawn wontons in a small bowl of clear, savoury broth.
Warm, wobbly egg custard in a crisp pastry shell, Hong Kong's favourite snack.
A sweet bun with a crackly sugar top, no pineapple in it, split hot with a slab of cold butter.
Strong black tea strained through a cloth and mixed with evaporated milk, silky and punchy.
Rice cooked in a clay pot until a crunchy crust forms, topped with sausage or meats and sweet soy.
A hot sheet of crisp edged bubbles, soft inside, eaten straight from the bag.

items.one: Crispy chilli crab and flaming duck, three minutes away
items.fits: Tue 27 dinner in Tsim Sha Tsui at 20:45, straight off the Avenue of Stars. Book a 21:00 table so you are not rushed after the cruise.

items.one: Classic wonton noodles in Jordan, open past midnight
items.fits: Tue 27 dinner if you would rather keep it casual: open to 00:30, no booking, and on the way to Temple Street if you have the energy. Also works Thu 29 before the market.

items.one: Michelin starred Cantonese, 25 floors above the harbour
items.fits: Wed 28 big dinner at 19:30. A short taxi down from the Peak, and the Mandarin Oriental is a five minute walk from the bars. The pick for views and occasion.

items.one: Apple wood Peking duck in a glamorous bank basement
items.fits: Wed 28 big dinner at 19:30. The pick for the best duck and the most theatre. Pre-order the duck when you book.

items.one: Loud, fun modern Cantonese in SoHo
items.fits: Wed 28 big dinner if you want a party rather than polish. Right in SoHo, so the bars are steps away afterwards.

items.one: Stocking strained milk tea and a pork chop bun
items.fits: Wed 28 at 14:00, right at the bottom of Graham Street Market as you arrive in Central. Or Thu 29 for a quick lunch. Closed Sundays, which is no problem for you.

items.one: Michelin starred roast goose on noodles
items.fits: Thu 29 lunch in Central at 14:00, off the train from Tung Chung. Hong Kong Station to Stanley Street is about ten minutes' walk, and 14:00 misses the lunch rush.

items.one: The city's best egg tart, sourdough crust, with coffee
items.fits: Thu 29 egg tart and coffee stop at 16:15. Up Hollywood Road from Man Mo Temple to Staunton Street, then down to the Star Ferry for 17:00. Takeaway, so eat it on the escalator steps.

items.one: Claypot rice on Temple Street, crisp crust and all
items.fits: Thu 29 Temple Street dinner at 19:30. Order the claypots first, they take 20 minutes, then browse the stalls after.

items.one: Old style yum cha with trolleys and harbour views
items.fits: Fri 30 yum cha at 12:30, the classic trolley option. Star Ferry across, then five minutes' walk. Call to book or arrive by 12:15. Back by Star Ferry for the spare window.

items.one: Refined Michelin dim sum at The Peninsula
items.fits: Fri 30 yum cha at 12:30, the upscale option. Ten minutes' walk from the hotel, so no harbour crossing on your last day.

items.one: Dim sum on the 2nd floor of your own hotel
items.fits: Fri 30 yum cha at 12:30, the near TST option: zero travel, and the easy choice if the pool runs long. Also a fallback dinner on any night.

items.one: Cantonese roast meats in Elements, below Ozone
items.fits: Fri 30 dinner at 19:15, straight down from Ozone in the same building. Tell them you need to leave by 20:15 for the airport.

items.one: Hot egg waffle from a Michelin street food counter
items.fits: Any afternoon or evening walk near the hotel. Good on Tue 27 after the promenade, or Fri 30 in the spare window.

items.one: Pineapple bun with a slab of butter, the original
items.fits: Thu 29 after Temple Street for supper: two MTR stops north and open to 23:30. Or a breakfast swap for the lounge on Wed 28.

items.one: The World's Best Bar 2025, walk-in only
items.fits: Wed 28 bars in Central, after dinner. Expect to queue, it is part of the fun. Ten minutes' walk from SoHo or Central.

items.one: Award winning agave bar, tequila and mezcal
items.fits: Wed 28 bars in Central. Drop by at about 19:15 on the way to dinner to put your name on the waitlist, then come back after.

items.one: Harbour view cocktails at the Four Seasons
items.fits: Wed 28 if you want a seat and a view rather than a queue. Two minutes from the Star Ferry pier, so it works before the ferry home.

items.one: Dark spirits and live jazz at the Rosewood
items.fits: Tue 27 late, or Thu 29 at 21:30 instead of going straight back to the hotel. Ten minutes' walk along the waterfront.

items.one: Harbour view bar at the top of your hotel
items.fits: Any evening at 20:00 for the light show, or a rainy afternoon. Handy on Fri 30 if Ozone is clouded in.

items.one: Chinese art with harbour windows, free entry
items.fits: Fri 30 spare window at 14:00, five minutes from the hotel. Closed Thursday.

items.one: Timber nunnery and a Tang style garden
items.fits: Fri 30 spare window at 14:00, about 25 minutes by MTR. Go early in the window so the nunnery halls are still open.

items.one: Street stalls, sneakers and the Goldfish Market

areas.notes: Book this week: the Wed 28 big dinner (Man Wah, Mott 32 or Ho Lee Fook; pre-order the duck at Mott 32), Hutong if you want it for Tue 27, and Spring Moon if that is your Fri 30 yum cha. The Chairman was named Asia's best in 2026 but now opens for lunch only and is very hard to book, so it is not an option for Wed 28 dinner. No Happy Valley races on your dates: Wed 28 is a Sha Tin meeting. Hong Kong Museum of Art is closed on Thursdays, so keep it for Friday. Coa is closed Mondays and Lan Fong Yuen on Sundays, neither of which clashes. Bar Leone and Coa take no bookings, so expect to queue on Wed 28. Hing Kee, Mak Man Kee and the Temple Street stalls are cash only. Some opening hours here come from older listings (Mammy Pancake, Lei Garden at Elements, Hutong): check Google Maps the day before.
